data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕清仓拍卖店和二手商品店的讨论，包括其运营模式、商品质量、价格策略以及整体经济环境对其影响的多角度分析。

不同观点：
• **[jjkaczor]** 分享了自己在清仓拍卖店的经历，起初能以极低价格买到高质量商品，但随着更多人参与，价格上涨，商品质量下降，甚至一些店铺已经关闭。他认为整体经济放缓可能是导致商品减少的原因。
• **[mdip]** 描述了自己所在地区类似的店铺，认为这些店铺依然有大量库存，并且能以较低价格买到高价值商品，尽管需要花费更多时间和精力。
• **[neilv]** 提出这些店铺可能在挑选有价值的商品放在自己的线上商店出售，而不是全部放在实体店中，这种做法可能影响消费者的购物体验。
• **[nancyminusone]** 对店铺中的商品质量持批评态度，认为大部分商品都是垃圾，难以理解为什么会有人购买。
• **[tra3]** 表达了对退货行为的不适感，宁愿不买也不愿意退货，这与其他人对购物和退货的态度形成对比。
• **[jccalhoun]** 也认为这些店铺中的商品多为廉价和无用的物品，导致店铺难以维持经营。
• **[chime]** 引用视频讨论了这些商品处理背后的环境影响，质疑这些商品是否真的避免了进入垃圾填埋场。
• **[bravesoul2]** 认为在清仓店省钱需要极大的耐心和纪律，建议有计划地购物以避免买到无用商品。
• **[twright]** 通过在亚马逊套利公司的实习经历，指出这些店铺提供了一个寻找已生产商品的场所。
• **[tantalor]** 讨论了关税对进口商品和清仓店可能产生的影响，认为经济冲击可能会促进二手经济的发展。
• **[ryukoposting]** 提到自己当地的 surplus 店通过 GoFundMe 筹集资金，担心这种模式会取代传统店铺。
• **[twic]** 和 **[jp57]** 则分别以幽默的方式对店铺的定价策略和购物体验进行了评论。

补充讨论：
• 商品的来源和店铺的运营模式是讨论的重点，包括店铺如何挑选商品以及潜在的环境影响。
• 价格策略和经济环境的变化对这些店铺的影响也是讨论的核心，涉及到买家费用、关税和整体经济放缓等因素。
• 争议的焦点在于这些店铺的商品质量和价格是否值得消费者花费时间和精力去寻找和购买。

44192995.article_content:
Jen Kinney
Capital
Seven Days At The Bin Store
By
Jen Kinney
9:02 AM EDT on June 4, 2025
Share on Bluesky
Share on Reddit
Share on WhatsApp
Share on Email
150
Comments
This spring, a new business opened on the main drag of my West Philadelphia neighborhood, provoking both excitement and trepidation.
“I saw it just the other day and feared it,” one friend texted. “Like what the actual fuck is that shit,” said another. “Why?!!!” said a third. “Who is that for?”
Until last summer, the corner storefront at Baltimore Avenue and S. Melville Street was a moderately overpriced hipster vintage store. After it closed, it sat empty for nearly a year. Then, in March, it sprang to life.
A “grand opening” banner went up over the door. A miniature wacky inflatable tube man flailed around outside. Posters with the logos for Walmart, Amazon, Costco, and Best Buy covered the windows, declaring “CRAZY DEALS, AMAZING BINZ.” I had to check it out.
AMAZING BINZ is on the first floor of a rowhome, narrow and long. There’s one central aisle, and on either side, big wooden tray tables—the proverbial binz—overflowing with undifferentiated piles of consumer
stuff
: unopened Halloween costumes, an ice mold shaped like a penis, a banner of many glittery penises wearing grass skirts, a staggering number of “reusable hot and cold gel compression sleeve[s] for elbow,” a single loose pregnancy test, something called Wokaar for “waxing the nose beard.”
At least half the products are still in boxes, and there are signs on the walls warning customers to NOT OPEN THE BOXES, so you have to scan the barcode with your phone or decipher clipped product descriptions: “module stool,” “gratitude journal,” “Xmas tea light green.” But the great innovation of Amazing Binz is its pricing structure, which is splashed across the facade in Spanish and English and makes good on the promise of CRAZY DEALS. On Fridays, when the bins are freshly stocked, everything costs $10. On Saturdays, $8. Sundays: $6. Mondays: $4. Tuesdays: $2. Wednesdays: $1. Thursday is bin store Sabbath, when the shop is closed and restocked.
The store is like nothing else on the block, which boasts, among other things, a yoga studio, two vape shops, a volunteer-run book store
and
a Marxist reading room, and no fewer than four Ethiopian joints.
Where did all this stuff come from? Who opened this store, and why? Is it profitable? What does it mean for the uneven gentrification of Baltimore Avenue and West Philadelphia? I decided to spend a week visiting Amazing Binz every day. Here is what I found.
Thursday: Restock Day
On Thursdays, Amazing Binz is closed. One of the owners, Ahmed, has graciously allowed me to observe the restock. Overall, Ahmed has been very gracious about my fixation on his store.
When I arrive at 10:30 a.m., he’s smoking a cigarette and nervously awaiting a delivery truck with 18 pallets of mixed merchandise from Target. Amazing Binz gets its inventory from major corporations’ overstock and returned products, taking advantage of the vast weird world of “reverse logistics.”
“ You've got the front end, where you order the product, it comes into the port, it goes to a warehouse, to a store, and then to our front door,” says Cathy Roberson, a researcher at the Reverse Logistics Association, an industry trade group. “What if once it hits our front door, we don't like it, or it's broken or something? That's the reverse part. ”
Returns, repairs, refurbished products, and even recalls fall into the purview of reverse logistics. They are joined there by products that never made it to a consumer because the season ended, or a box was a little dented, or the purchaser never picked up their order, or a retailer was just running out of room in their warehouse.
That pile of excess stuff is growing. About 17 percent of all merchandise gets returned, according to the National Retail Federation. That’s up from just eight percent in 2019. For online purchases, it’s almost 30 percent.
Liquidators are nothing new: T.J. Maxx, Ocean State Job Lot, Nordstrom Rack. But as the scale of the excess grows, the reverse logistics industry is expanding, and methods of disposal are diversifying. Some corporations, like Amazon, do their own reselling through a
bulk liquidation page
. There are middlemen like
B-Stock
, an eBay-like site where anyone can shop for truckloads of unwanted stuff. Influencers are buying pallets to unbox on stream, capitalizing on both the goods and the views. It’s a whole universe of brokers, wholesalers, and secondhand retail all trying to claw back a little bit of money from the growing pile. That’s where Amazing Binz comes in.
“The goal for all the reverse logistics stuff,” says Roberson, “is to keep things out of the landfill.”
Today, Ahmed is expecting half a truckload with about 3,500 to 4,500 individual pieces, ranging from kitchen appliances to toys to clothing; he doesn’t know exactly what. The semi-truck pulls up right on time, and Ahmed unloads it with a forklif

HyperDX
HyperDX
, a core component of
ClickStack
, helps engineers
quickly figure out why production is broken by making it easy to search &
visualize logs and traces on top of any ClickHouse cluster (imagine Kibana, for
ClickHouse).
Documentation
•
Chat on Discord
•
Live Demo
•
Bug Reports
•
Contributing
•
Website
🕵️ Correlate/search logs, metrics, session replays and traces all in one place
📝 Schema agnostic, works on top of your existing ClickHouse schema
🔥 Blazing fast searches & visualizations optimized for ClickHouse
🔍 Intuitive full-text search and property search syntax (ex.
level:err
),
SQL optional!
📊 Analyze trends in anomalies with event deltas
🔔 Set up alerts in just a few clicks
📈 Dashboard high cardinality events without a complex query language
{
Native JSON string querying
⚡ Live tail logs and traces to always get the freshest events
🔭 OpenTelemetry supported out of the box
⏱️ Monitor health and performance from HTTP requests to DB queries (APM)
Spinning Up HyperDX
HyperDX can be deployed as part of ClickStack, which includes ClickHouse,
HyperDX, OpenTelemetry Collector and MongoDB.
docker run -p 8080:8080 -p 4317:4317 -p 4318:4318 docker.hyperdx.io/hyperdx/hyperdx-all-in-one
Afterwards, you can visit
http://localhost:8080
to access the HyperDX UI.
If you already have an existing ClickHouse instance, want to use a single
container locally, or are looking for production deployment instructions, you
can view the different deployment options in our
deployment docs
.
If your server is behind a firewall, you'll need to open/forward port 8080,
8000 and 4318 on your firewall for the UI, API and OTel collector
respectively.
We recommend at least 4GB of RAM and 2 cores for testing.
Hosted ClickHouse Cloud
You can also deploy HyperDX with ClickHouse Cloud, you can
sign up for free
and get started in
just minutes.
Instrumenting Your App
To get logs, metrics, traces, session replay, etc into HyperDX, you'll need to
instrument your app to collect and send telemetry data over to your HyperDX
instance.
We provide a set of SDKs and integration options to make it easier to get
started with HyperDX, such as
Browser
,
Node.js
,
and
Python
You can find the full list in
our docs
.
OpenTelemetry
Additionally, HyperDX is compatible with
OpenTelemetry
, a vendor-neutral standard for
instrumenting your application backed by CNCF. Supported languages/platforms
include:
Kubernetes
Javascript
Python
Java
Go
Ruby
PHP
.NET
Elixir
Rust
(Full list
here
)
Once HyperDX is running, you can point your OpenTelemetry SDK to the
OpenTelemetry collector spun up at
http://localhost:4318
.
Contributing
We welcome all contributions! There's many ways to contribute to the project,
including but not limited to:
Opening a PR (
Contribution Guide
)
Submitting feature requests or bugs
Improving our product or contribution documentation
Voting on
open issues
or
contributing use cases to a feature request
Motivation
Our mission is to help engineers ship reliable software. To enable that, we
believe every engineer needs to be able to easily leverage production telemetry
to quickly solve burning production issues.
However, in our experience, the existing tools we've used tend to fall short in
a few ways:
They're expensive, and the pricing has failed to scale with TBs of telemetry
becoming the norm, leading to teams aggressively cutting the amount of data
they can collect.
They're hard to use, requiring full-time SREs to set up, and domain experts
to use confidently.
They requiring hopping from tool to tool (logs, session replay, APM,
exceptions, etc.) to stitch together the clues yourself.
We hope you give HyperDX in ClickStack a try an

data.title: Google restricts Android sideloading
data.author: fsflover
data.article_summary: Google近期通过限制Android系统的侧载功能，以增强安全性、防止诈骗和恶意软件。在新加坡的试点项目中，通过网页浏览器、消息应用或文件管理器侧载的某些请求敏感权限的应用将被阻止安装。同时，Google推出了Play Integrity API，允许开发者限制侧载应用的功能，鼓励用户通过Google Play商店安装应用。这些举措引发了对用户自主权、创新限制和市场竞争的担忧，批评者认为此举使Android更接近苹果iOS的封闭生态。对此，Purism推出运行PureOS的Librem 5手机，提供安全、隐私尊重和数据自主的替代方案，不依赖企业应用商店和侵入式API。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google在部分地区和情况下限制 sideloading 应用的功能，引发了关于用户自由、安全性以及技术实现的讨论。

不同观点：
• tdeck：认为一些评论忽视了普通用户的技术水平，高级用户可以通过技术手段解决限制，但普通用户很难做到。对普通用户来说，限制 sideloading 是有意义的，因为这可以防止恶意软件和诈骗。
• Aurornis：指出限制主要针对新加坡的一个试点项目，且仅限于某些敏感权限的应用。高级用户仍然可以找到方法 sideload 应用，这不算对自由的严重侵犯，更多的是对普通用户的保护。
• jeroenhd：认为这个限制早在一年多前就已宣布，质疑相关博客文章的发布时机。提到可以通过关闭 Play Protect 绕过限制，但同时也引用了新加坡警方的案例，说明诈骗犯如何利用 sideloaded 应用进行诈骗。
• gbin：虽然主张用户应有对自己设备的最大控制权，但也提到 DJI 强制用户 sideload 应用的例子，指出这种做法可能带来的安全隐患。
• Zigurd：认为 Google 的设计是合理且有意义的，限制 sideloading 只是增加了恶意软件运行的难度，而不是完全禁止。
• danieldk：指出 GrapheneOS 提供了 Google Android 的安全优势，但 Google 拒绝让其使用 Play Integrity API 的硬件认证功能，导致某些应用无法使用，批评 Google 的双重标准。
• londons_explore：解释新加坡的特殊情况，指出诈骗和身份交易问题严重，限制敏感权限的应用是必要的。
• rafram：认为相关讨论是软文，没有具体分析。
• nikodunk：主张支持开源项目如 postmarketOS，认为继续 fork Android 不是长久之计。
• AstralStorm：建议仅在调试模式和用户明确许可的情况下允许 sideloading，认为这是更安全的方案。
• mfuzzey：关心替代应用商店如 F-droid 是否会受到影响，提到 Ingress 玩家常用的非官方应用。
• throitallaway：认为 Google 应专注于完善沙盒和权限模型，而不是限制应用来源。
• qbane：个人习惯 sideload 应用，无法想象无法 sideload 的情况，可能会因此而 root 设备。
• EwanToo：指出相关新闻早在2024年就已发布，质疑讨论的时效性。
• mcflubbins：关心 Librem 5 手机的基本功能和可靠性，特别是短信和通话功能以及电池寿命。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于用户自由与设备安全的平衡。高级用户认为限制不应存在，普通用户则可能从限制中受益。
• 具体技术实现如 GrapheneOS 和 Play Integrity API 的使用问题也被提及，显示出对 Google 政策的不满。
• 新加坡的试点项目被多次提到，显示出该项目在讨论中的重要性。
• 对 sideloading 的安全风险有多个例子支持，如 DJI 应用和诈骗案例。
• 对替代方案如 postmarketOS 和 Librem 5 的讨论显示出社区对开放性和安全性的持续关注。

• Aurornis：指出限制主要针对新加坡的一个试点项目，且仅限于某些敏感权限的应用。高级用户仍然可以找到方法 sideload 应用，这不算对自由的严重侵犯，更多的是对普通用户的保护。
• jeroenhd：认为这个限制早在一年多前就已宣布，质疑相关博客文章的发布时机。提到可以通过关闭 Play Protect 绕过限制，但同时也引用了新加坡警方的案例，说明诈骗犯如何利用 sideloaded 应用进行诈骗。
• gbin：虽然主张用户应有对自己设备的最大控制权，但也提到 DJI 强制用户 sideload 应用的例子，指出这种做法可能带来的安全隐患。
• Zigurd：认为 Google 的设计是合理且有意义的，限制 sideloading 只是增加了恶意软件运行的难度，而不是完全禁止。
• danieldk：指出 GrapheneOS 提供了 Google Android 的安全优势，但 Google 拒绝让其使用 Play Integrity API 的硬件认证功能，导致某些应用无法使用，批评 Google 的双重标准。
• londons_explore：解释新加坡的特殊情况，指出诈骗和身份交易问题严重，限制敏感权限的应用是必要的。
• rafram：认为相关讨论是软文，没有具体分析。
• nikodunk：主张支持开源项目如 postmarketOS，认为继续 fork Android 不是长久之计。
• AstralStorm：建议仅在调试模式和用户明确许可的情况下允许 sideloading，认为这是更安全的方案。
• mfuzzey：关心替代应用商店如 F-droid 是否会受到影响，提到 Ingress 玩家常用的非官方应用。
• throitallaway：认为 Google 应专注于完善沙盒和权限模型，而不是限制应用来源。
• qbane：个人习惯 sideload 应用，无法想象无法 sideload 的情况，可能会因此而 root 设备。
• EwanToo：指出相关新闻早在2024年就已发布，质疑讨论的时效性。
• mcflubbins：关心 Librem 5 手机的基本功能和可靠性，特别是短信和通话功能以及电池寿命。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于用户自由与设备安全的平衡。高级用户认为限制不应存在，普通用户则可能从限制中受益。
• 具体技术实现如 GrapheneOS 和 Play Integrity API 的使用问题也被提及，显示出对 Google 政策的不满。
• 新加坡的试点项目被多次提到，显示出该项目在讨论中的重要性。
• 对 sideloading 的安全风险有多个例子支持，如 DJI 应用和诈骗案例。
• 对替代方案如 postmarketOS 和 Librem 5 的讨论显示出社区对开放性和安全性的持续关注。

data.title: Programming language Dino and its implementation
data.author: 90s_dev
data.article_summary: Dino是一种高级脚本编程语言，结合了面向对象和函数式编程的特性。它由Vladimir Makarov开发，最初于1993年为俄罗斯游戏公司ANIMATEK设计，之后经过多次修订。Dino具有多精度整数、异构可扩展数组、关联表、数组切片、模式匹配、Unicode 8支持等特性。其并发处理通过纤维（fiber）实现，类似于绿色线程，比OS线程更快且具有确定性行为。Dino的类是一种特殊函数，支持多重继承和动态调度。其字节码编译器和解释器支持JIT和类型推断，性能可与Python、Ruby、JavaScript等语言媲美。Dino的实现包括多种工具和优化，目标是提供一种高效、安全且易用的编程语言。

Programming language Dino and its implementation
Develepment version of future release 0.98
Vladimir Makarov,
vmakarov@gcc.gnu.org
Apr 2, 2016
Description Layout
Introduction to Dino
History
Dino as a high-level scripting language
Dino as a functional language
Dino as an object-oriented language
Dino Implementation
Overall Structure
Used implementation tools
Byte code compiler (optimizations)
Byte code Interpreter (GC, Concurrency, REPL)
JIT, Type inference
Performance comparison with Python, PyPy, Ruby, JS, Scala, OCAML
on x86-64, AARH64, ARM, PPC64.
Some history
1993: Original language design and implementation
Was used in russian computer game company ANIMATEK as a simple
scripting language for describing dinosaurus movements
1998, 2002, 2007, 2016 : Major language and implementation revisions
This document describes the current state of Dino language and
its implementation.
The first taste of Dino
Eratosthenes sieve:
var i, prime, k, count = 0, SieveSize = 8191, flags = [SieveSize : 1];
for (i = 0; i < SieveSize; i++)
if (flags[i]) {
prime = i + i + 3;
k = i + prime;
for (;;) {
if (k >= SieveSize)
break;
flags[k] = 0;
k += prime;
}
count++;
}
putln (count);
DINO as a scripting language
Dino aims to look like C language
High-Level scripting object-oriented language:
Multi-precision integers
Heterogeneous extensible arrays, array slices
Associative tables with possibility to delete elements
Powerful and safe class composition operation for (multiple)
inheritance and traits description
First class functions, classes, and fibers with closures,
anonymous functions, classes, fibers
Exception handling
Concurrency
Pattern matching
Unicode 8 support
Arrays and Tables
Associative tables
elements can be added and deleted
elements can be any values, e.g. other tables
Implemented as hash tables without buckets for compactness
and data locality
Secondary hash for conflict resolutions
Murmur hash function for most values
Array Slices
Eratosthenes sieve with slices:
var i, prime, count = 0, SieveSize = 8191, flags = [SieveSize : 1];
for (i = 0; i < SieveSize; i++)
if (flags[i]) {
prime = i + i + 3;
flags[i + prime:SieveSize:prime] = 0;
count++;
}
putln (count);
Functions
Example:
fun even;
fun odd  (i) {i == 0 ? 0 : even (i - 1);}
fun even (i) {i == 0 ? 1 : odd (i - 1);}
putln (odd (1_000_000));
Anonymous functions:
filter (fun (a) {a > 0;}, v);
fold (fun (a, b) {a * b;}, v, 1);
Function closures:
fun incr (base) {fun (incr) {base + incr;}}
Threads
Fiber: a function with concurrent execution
fiber t (n) {for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) putln (i);}
t(100); // the following code don't wait for t finish
for (var i = 0; i < 1000; i++) putln (“main”, i);
Implemented as green threads:
Much faster than OS threads with Global Interpreter Lock (Python/Ruby)
Deterministic behaviour and automatic deadlock recognition
Plans to implement through OS threads without GIL for parallelism
There is a low level sync-statement wait
wait (cond) [stmt];
Simple statements are atomic
Object orientation
Class is just a special type of function:
Returns closure, public visibility by default
class num (i) {fun print {put (i);}}
class binop (l, r) { fun print_op;
fun print {l.print(); print_op (); r.print ();}
}
Special class/function composition:
emulates (multiple) inheritance, traits, and dynamic dispatching
class add (l, r) {
use binop former l, r later print_op;
fun print_op {put (“ + “);}
}
Object orientation -- continuation
A safe and powerful way to support object orientation
Declarations of class mentioned in
use
are inlayed
Declarations before the use rewrite corresponding inlayed
declarations mentioned in
former
-clause
Declarations after the use rewrite corresponding inserted
declarations mentioned in
later

data.title: Aurora, a foundation model for the Earth system
data.author: rmason
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软Aurora天气预测模型的发布及其相关技术与应用

不同观点：
• magicalhippo：对深度神经网络在解决量子物理问题上的成功表示认可，并认为其在天气预测中的良好表现并不意外。同时提供了Aurora模型相关的发布链接和资源。
   
• sieste：认为AI基础模型不应被简单宣传为传统物理预测的替代品，强调AI天气模型依赖于ERA5再分析数据（结合观测和数值模型预测），建议更多强调AI与物理模型的协同作用，而非单纯比较优劣。

• xnx：提问Aurora模型是否与谷歌的模型类似，并附上了谷歌相关研究的链接。

• scottcha：基于使用经验，对Aurora模型的优点进行了总结，包括开源、可配置性强、免费非商业使用、与开发者互动良好等。

• goochphd：提到了一些关于Aurora项目的演示，指出其在中小尺度天气现象和极端天气预测上的优势，以及在训练高分辨率数据空间方面的技术突破。

• dmillard：提到Aurora系统的两位原作者离开微软创立了Silurian.ai，建议关注这一新项目。

• croemer：提供了与Aurora相关的Nature论文链接。

• Lyngbakr：指出AI天气模型（如GraphCast、Aardvark、NeuralGCM、Aurora等）的研发团队常包括微软和谷歌的员工，质疑这些公司内部的跨团队合作是否促进了技术进步，或者这些模型开发是否完全独立。

• nxobject：提出Aurora模型是否可以用于制作沙盒模拟游戏的设想。

• waltbosz：提到Aurora模型的命名让他联想到阿西莫夫的小说《基地与地球》中的行星Aurora。

• roger_：表示一直关注GitHub上的wesselb，很高兴看到其工作获得更多关注。

• dunkeltaenzer：质疑为何在讨论中为付费墙内容打广告。

补充讨论：
• 关于Aurora模型与谷歌模型的比较（xnx和goochphd的观点）。
• 关于AI模型与传统物理模型关系的争议（sieste的观点）。
• 对Aurora模型技术细节和应用潜力的探讨（goochphd和scottcha的观点）。
• 对Aurora模型团队成员流动及新项目成立的关注（dmillard的观点）。
• 对模型命名与文化作品关联的联想（waltbosz的观点）。
• 对付费墙内容在讨论中出现的质疑（dunkeltaenzer的观点）。

data.title: Understanding the PURL Specification (Package URL)
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Package URL (PURL) 是一个开放标准，用于跨不同软件生态系统唯一标识软件包。PURL 由 Philippe Ombredanne 于 2017 年创建，是一种特殊格式的 URL，描述软件包在注册表中的位置或身份。其结构类似于网页 URL，包含类型、名称、命名空间、版本、限定符和子路径等字段。PURL 已成为软件物料清单（SBOM）的重要组成部分，用于唯一标识软件组件。它支持多种编程语言和包管理器，如 npm、PyPI、Maven、Docker 等，并可在 SBOM 中作为组件的唯一标识符。尽管某些字段是可选的，但在实际使用中对唯一标识包至关重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PURL（Package URL）标准的实用性、设计及其在不同场景下的适用性。

不同观点：
• **alcroito**：认为PURL在追踪未托管在如Conan.io等注册库的自托管C/C++原生库时缺乏有效支持，特别是如Qt或KDE等库。目前似乎只能使用"generic"类型加上vcs_url限定符，这导致开放工具难以追踪这些库的漏洞。
• **emddudley**：指出PURL与Internet Archive管理的PURL不同，提醒大家注意区分。
• **kdeldycke**：分享了一个支持PURL的项目Meta Package Manager，展示了如何使用PURL来安装包和管理软件物料清单（SBOM）。
• **zzo38computer**：提出PURL存在的几个问题，包括缺少加密哈希、没有区分接口和实现、以及缺少某些包类型的限定符示例。
• **dedicate**：认为PURL使SBOMs在开源中更具实用性，而不仅仅是基于CPEs的“最佳猜测”。
• **account42**：质疑PURL的命名，认为它只识别包而不定位包，应该叫PURI。
• **quibono**：认为PURL比CPE更易用，特别是在软件不符合传统的供应商/产品划分时。
• **RS-232**：对PURL中的命名空间属性使用点符号表示不满，认为应该使用kebab case。
• **rahkiin**：询问PURL如何处理未托管在Docker的Docker镜像或自定义npm注册库。
• **heavenlyhash**：对包名称中包含斜杠的情况提出疑问，特别是Golang包的处理方式。
• **CodingKing**：认为PURL应该是一个注册的URN，而不是URL，因为URL表示位置，URN表示身份。

The Package URL (PURL) specification is an open standard for uniquely identifying software packages across different ecosystems. It was
created in 2017
by Philippe Ombredanne, an open source tooling maintainer who needed a better way to standardize references to software packages.
A PURL is a specially formatted URL that describes a software package's location or identity in a package registry. It encodes the package type (e.g. npm, Maven, PyPI), the name (and optional group or namespace), version, and other qualifiers in a single string.
PURL's purpose is to provide a simple, universal identifier for software components, making it easy to track and share what components are in your software. Although PURL has several important use cases, the combination of its universal properties and machine-readability in particular have made it an essential part of enabling the modern SBOM landscape.
In this blog, we'll explain in more depth how PURL works (including differences in different ecosystems), how it’s used in
SBOMs
, how it compares to CPE and other component identifiers, and more.
How PURL Works
A Package URL is structured similarly to a web URL, with multiple components separated by specific symbols. The general syntax is:
pkg:<type>/
<namespace>/
<name>@<version>
?<qualifiers>#<subpath>
Each part of this string has a specific meaning, which we'll outline below; you can also reference the
PURL Spec’s GitHub README
and
PURL Types page
for additional context.
Required Fields
scheme
:
The scheme is always
pkg
, indicating a package URL (just like
http
or
https
in web URLs). This constant prefix helps tools recognize a PURL immediately.
type
:
The package
type
or ecosystem, such as
npm
,
maven
,
pypi
,
nuget
,
gem
(RubyGems), etc.
name
:
The name of the package (artifact or module name).
Optional Fields
namespace
:
An optional namespace or group for the package, which is specific to the ecosystem. For example, in Maven, this would be the groupId (
org.apache.logging.log4j
), in Docker it might be an image owner, or in GitHub it could be an organization/user. Not all ecosystems have namespaces.
version
:
The version of the package (if applicable). Not all PURLs include a version (e.g. if you want to refer to a package in general), but typically an SBOM or vulnerability reference will include a specific version here.
qualifiers
:
Additional key-value pairs to further qualify the package, prefixed by
?
and separated by
&
. Qualifiers are optional and depend on the package type.
subpath
:
An optional subpath within the package, appended after a
#
. This can point to a specific file or directory inside the package. It's used when you need to reference a particular piece of a package's content.
It's important to note that while the above fields are optional when determining whether a PURL is valid, in practice, they play very important roles in making it possible to uniquely identify a package. Specifically, namespace and version are important for all ecosystems, and qualifier and subpath are important in particular for Linux ecosystems.
To help bring everything together, let's consider an example PURL for a Maven Central artifact:
pkg:maven/
org.apache.logging.log4j/
log4j-core@2.14.1
This identifies the Apache Log4j Core library version 2.14.1 from the Maven ecosystem (groupId org.apache.logging.log4j, artifactId log4j-core).
PURL Ecosystem Coverage
PURL supports a broad array of programming language ecosystems and package managers out of the box. Common types include
npm
(Node.js/JavaScript packages),
pypi
(Python packages),
maven
(Java artifacts),
nuget
(.NET packages),
gem
(Ruby Gems),
golang
(Go modules),
cargo
(Rust crates),
docker
(container images), and system packages like
deb
(Debian/Ubuntu) or
rpm
(Fedora/RedHat).
Each type definition specifies how to interpret the namespace and qualifiers for that ecosystem. For instance, Docker PURLs use the image name as the name and tag or digest as the version (e.g.
pkg:docker/nginx@1.21.0
or by digest), and may use a qualifier for the registry URL.
There's even a
generic
type as a catch-all for things that don't fit an existing ecosystem (for example, a proprietary or legacy component) or for ecosystems that build custom distributions, such as yocto or buildroot. We should note, however, that SBOM and software composition analysis tools vary widely in their ability to understand generic PURLs, so we do recommend you talk to your current (or prospective) vendor if this is an important feature for you.
PURL and SBOMs
The most common Package URL use case that we see today is the role it plays in enabling the SBOM (software bill of materials) ecosystem. SBOMs are essentially a list of components (libraries, frameworks, modules, etc.) that make up a software product, and PURLs play a critical role in SBOMs by acting as the unique identifiers for each component.

data.article_summary: 文章主要探讨了技术创新之间的相互关联，特别是枪械与相机之间的联系。作者Étienne Fortier-Dubois解释了相机和枪械共享一些术语（如“装载”、“瞄准”、“射击”）的原因，可能源于人们将枪械操作的语言用于描述操作相似的相机。文章追溯了电影摄影技术的起源，指出托马斯·爱迪生和其实验室发明的电影摄影机（kinetograph）受到了法国科学家艾蒂安-朱尔·马雷的瞬时摄影研究启发，而马雷的设计又受到了天文学家皮埃尔·詹森的“摄影左轮”启发。詹森的设备借鉴了左轮手枪的旋转机制，而这种机制可追溯到16世纪的枪械技术。作者强调，许多技术创新看似无关，实则彼此联系，并介绍了自己正在进行的项目——构建一个展示主要技术创新及其相互联系的时间线，称为“历史技术树”（historical tech tree）。

44161607.article_content:
The Universal Tech Tree
Étienne Fortier-Dubois
When we try and pick out any technology in isolation, we find it hitched, in some way, to every innovation that preceded it. (Except for the Oldowan hand axe. We had to start somewhere.)
What do firearms and cameras have in common? One answer is shared vocabulary: load, aim, shoot. The etymological origins of this relatedness are murky. People likely borrowed language about firearms — which are over 500 years older than photography — to talk about cameras, which are operated in a similar manner.  But in the case of the movie camera, the connection is concrete.
The first movie camera is generally considered to be the kinetograph, invented in 1891 by Thomas Edison and William Kennedy Dickson, an inventor at the Edison lab. Two years earlier, Edison had travelled to Paris to the Exposition Universelle of 1889, a world’s fair, to showcase his company’s phonograph. There, he met with Étienne-Jules Marey, a French scientist who had begun his career studying blood circulation, and who had developed an interest in chronophotography partly out of his work on physiology. Chronophotography consists of taking multiple photographs in quick succession to capture movement.
A famous early achievement of the technique is
The Horse in Motion
, a series of photographs taken by Eadweard Muybridge in 1878 that proved something Marey had asserted years earlier: For a brief moment in gallop, a horse has all four hooves off the ground. Encouraged by Muybridge, Marey developed an improved device to take chronophotographs. The resulting design, the “photographic gun,” featured a long barrel derived from existing firearms. We don’t know what transpired between Marey and Edison, but it seems likely that Marey’s design inspired the kinetograph. Coincidentally (or not), the Online Etymology Dictionary’s entry for “
shoot
” claims “the meaning ‘to photograph’ (especially a movie) is from 1890” — around the time of the kinetograph’s invention.
Marey himself had been inspired by the invention of another Frenchman, the astronomer Pierre Janssen. In 1874, hoping to capture images of the transit of Venus, Janssen created a device he called the “photographic revolver.” It looked like a large telescope. Inside, it hosted a complex camera that used a revolving apparatus to take several images in quick succession. The resulting eight seconds of the black dot of Venus moving across the sun disk are often recognized as the first motion picture in history.
1
Prior to Jansenn’s invention, revolving components had not been used in photography or astronomy. They came from the Colt Paterson revolver, a handgun popular in the U.S. since its mid-19th century creation by Samuel Colt. Thus, we can reconstruct a genealogical succession of ideas: Colt inspired Janssen, who inspired Marey, who likely inspired Edison (who then inspired the Lumière brothers and further developments in filmmaking).
We can go further back still. Colt improved the revolver and made its mass production commercially viable, but he did not invent it. Nor was it a particularly recent development: Guns with a revolving barrel have existed since the 16th century. A
German revolver
dates from 1597, but there are even older specimens. The
xun lei chong
, a Chinese revolving musket, also dates from this period.
It makes sense: The 1500s were a time of great innovation in firing mechanisms for muskets and arquebuses, with developments like the wheellock (which used a spinning metal wheel against pyrite to create sparks), snaplock (which struck flint against steel using a spring-loaded arm), and flintlock (which improved on the snaplock with a combined hammer-flint holder). Volley guns made of multiple cannons existed in England since at least the 1330s. These were descendants, in turn, of simpler cannons that stem from the invention of gunpowder in China in the 800s. It stands to reason that eventually
someone
in Europe would think of making a spinning mechanism to allow a weapon to fire multiple shots in quick succession.
And yet, if you’re anything like me, most of what you just read was probably surprising. We don’t typically associate revolvers with the 1500s, or, for that matter, with movie cameras.
The reason I learned about this — and dozens of anecdotes around other inventions — is that I have been working on a quixotic project to place all major technological innovations in history on a timeline, together with the connections between them. The goal is to situate stories like that of the revolver and camera in their historical context, notice patterns, and understand the logic of the history of technology. The result is an interactive visualization that I call
the historical tech tree
.
Étienne-Jules Marey, Bird Flight, Pelican, 1886.

data.title: Rare black iceberg spotted off Labrador coast could be 100k years old
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 2025年5月中旬，纽芬兰省卡博尼尔的渔民哈鲁尔·安东尼森在拉布拉多海岸捕虾时拍摄到了一座罕见的黑色冰山，引发社交媒体热议。这座冰山距离拉布拉多海岸超过100公里，呈现独特的钻石形状和黑色纹理。纪念大学的物理海洋学教授莱夫·塔拉索夫推测，这座冰山可能有上千年的历史，甚至可能达到10万年之久。他表示，冰山可能含有火山灰或千年积累的尘土，显示了冰的动态变化过程。冰流从格陵兰内部移动到海岸，形成冰山并最终漂至纽芬兰和拉布拉多。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：黑色冰山的出现及其相关科学、语言学和幽默讨论

不同观点：
• [HocusLocus] 认为如果自己是发现者，也会像Fisher Hallur Antoniussen一样拍照分享，显示出对这种罕见现象的兴趣和共鸣。
• [tickerticker] 从物理学角度分析，认为露出水面的部分呈球形，意味着水下部分巨大且对称，以保持这种直立状态。
• [tantalor] 以幽默方式建议在黑色冰山附近寻找“超级样本”，暗指可能有更多有趣的发现。
• [scoot] 提出严肃的科学问题，询问黑色冰山是否对科学家、地质学家、气候学家等有采样价值，反映出对科学研究潜力的关注。
• [bee_rider] 以幽默方式提问黑色冰山是否像黑色拉布拉多犬一样具有有助于游泳的特征（如蹼足）。
• [morkalork] 提出关于冰山年龄的问题，询问断裂的冰山是否会变得越来越老。
• [IncreasePosts] 认为由于黑色冰山颜色较深，可能更容易吸收太阳辐射而快速融化，质疑其是否真的有100,000年的历史。
• [dylan604] 对“鱼类收获者”（fish harvester）这一术语表示困惑，质疑是否因渔民一词不足以反映现代捕鱼量而改变术语。
• [m3kw9] 以幽默方式询问这种冰山何时会作为饮料出售，表现出对这种现象的娱乐性看法。
• [tromp] 对媒体使用“指数级更多”（exponentially more）这一术语表示不满，指出其数学上的不准确性，反映出对媒体用词严谨性的关注。

补充讨论：
• 评论中包含了幽默和科学探讨的混合，反映出公众对自然现象的多元化反应。
• 部分评论对媒体用词的准确性提出质疑，显示出对科学传播精确性的关注。
• 黑色冰山的科学价值和其物理特性成为讨论的焦点，部分评论者对其潜在研究价值表示兴趣。
• 评论中也包含了一些对术语和语言使用的讨论，反映出对现代术语变化的敏感性。

44193120.article_content:
NL
Rare black iceberg spotted off Labrador coast could be 100,000 years old, prof says
A fish harvester from Carbonear, N.L., snapped a photo of a black iceberg while fishing for shrimp of the coast of Labrador in mid May. It caused a sensation on social media, and impressed a Memorial University professor who says it's likely a very old piece of ice dating back thousands of years.
Berg may contain ice coloured by millennia of dirt — or even a meteorite strike
John Gaudi
·
CBC News
·
Posted: Jun 04, 2025 11:28 AM EDT | Last Updated: June 4
This black iceberg was spotted more than 100 kilometres off the coast of Labrador in mid-May. Fisher Hallur Antoniussen took a photo of it to show crewmates, but it quickly took off after being posted on social media.
(Submitted by Hallur Antoniussen)
Social Sharing
A rare black iceberg spotted off the coast of Labrador is making a splash on social media after a fish harvester living in Carbonear, N.L., took a photo of it while fishing for shrimp last month.
Originally from the Faroe Islands, Hallur Antoniussen was working with a crew on board the Saputi factory freezer trawler off the coast of Labrador in mid-May.
He'd never seen an iceberg like this one before.
"I have seen icebergs that are rolled, what they say have rolled in the beach with some rocks in it. This one here is completely different. It's not only that he is all black. He is almost ... in a diamond shape," Antoniussen said in an interview with CBC Radio's
Labrador Morning
.
He spotted the berg after going up the ship's crane when they were more than 100 kilometres offshore in the Hopedale channel, located between Nain and Hopedale.
A crew member had counted 47 icebergs in the area just the day before.
Antoniussen doesn't think it's a berg that tipped over — or rolled on the beach — picking up dirt and rocks after getting grounded. He's seen a lot of icebergs over his 50 years of fishing off of Greenland, and more recently off the Labrador coast since 1989.
The 64-year-old said it was hard to estimate the size of the iceberg at sea but figured it was at least three times the size of a regular bungalow.
He took a picture from roughly six kilometres away.
"It's something you don't see very often, and a camera is not something I run around [with] when I'm working. So, I just ran to my room and took my phone and snapped this picture," he said.
Memorial professor Lev Tarasov says ice from all over Greenland is converging toward its coastline, and then breaks off to form icebergs after reaching the water. Pictured here is the Kangerlussuaq Fjord outlet in Greenland.
(Submitted by Lev Tarasov )
Antoniussen said the berg looked like a rock with lots of really dark greys and black veins in it, and quickly ruled out that a shadow was being cast on it.
He took the photo to show other crew members on the fishing boat. Then Antoniussen posted it on Facebook, and it soon took off, garnering hundreds of comments after being shared around.
Commenters have mused about everything from aliens to precious metals, and even dinosaurs being hidden in the ice.
"It's an Oil Berg," said one poster.
"Looks like a giant [woolly] mammoth!" exclaimed another.
Antoniessen is clear: this is a real photo.
Other people wondered if the iceberg has volcanic ash in it, a result of some ancient eruption.
An impressive iceberg
Lev Tarasov, a Memorial University professor of physical oceanography, doesn't rule that last theory out completely.
Tarasov says there are volcanoes beneath the ice caps of Iceland, and while he's not exactly sure about volcanoes in Greenland, he added that scientists have measured hotspots in the landmass's central region.
Like Antoniussen, he hasn't seen an iceberg quite like this one before.
Tarasov observed smaller versions of the black iceberg during his fieldwork on the Kangerlussuaq Fjord in Greenland last summer — just not as impressive, he said.
Memorial University's Lev Tarasov is shown here conducted fieldwork in Greenland last summer. The professor says the black iceberg might contain ice that's more than 100,000 years old.
(Submitted by Lev Tarasov)
He guesses the ice in the berg is at least 1,000 years old, but could also be exponentially more ancient — even formed as many as 100,000 years ago.
Tarasov said ice from all over Greenland is slowly converging toward its coastline, and when it gets there, it breaks off to form icebergs.
Those icebergs can take one to three years before reaching the Newfoundland and Labrador coastline.
A terrestrial journey
Tarasov says it's a reminder just how dynamic ice can be.
Ice streams, also known as outlet glaciers, move much faster than other parts of the ice sheet; they carry ice from the interior, traveling through deep valleys or channels out to the coast.
They pick up rocks and dirt along the way.
"There's parts of the ice that are actually flowing up to 20 kilometres per year, which would mean that ... the ice is moving maybe a few metres every hour," Tarasov said.

data.author: ChrisArchitect
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了摄影应用**!Camera**，主打专业的摄影体验。该应用拥有全3D相机界面，具备动态光效、自定义触感，模拟真实相机手感。其**SuperRaw™**处理技术保留照片的自然颗粒，支持保存为DNG和Apple ProRaw格式。用户无需后期编辑即可直接分享照片，应用内置3D LUTs（色彩查找表）实现专业级色彩校正。此外，用户可自定义相机设置，手动控制曝光、对焦等参数，并通过**Precision Focus Ring**精确对焦。应用注重隐私，不收集用户数据，并由会员支持运营。目前该应用在iPhone和iPad上可用，但暂时缺货。

data.title: Gemini-2.5-pro-preview-06-05
data.author: jcuenod
data.article_summary: Google推出了Gemini 2.5系列模型，包括Gemini 2.5 Pro和2.5 Flash，具备更强的推理能力和多模态处理能力。Gemini 2.5 Pro引入了"Deep Think"模式，显著提升了编码性能和复杂任务处理能力，支持创建交互式网页应用和动画模拟等。新模型在多种基准测试中表现优异，尤其在推理、编码生成和长文本处理方面。此外，Gemini 2.5还增强了音频输出和可视化能力，使其在表达和互动上更加自然和高效。模型的性能和准确性均有显著提升，同时价格和效率也更加优化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Google的Gemini模型及其与竞争对手（如OpenAI的ChatGPT和Claude）在性能、市场竞争和用户体验方面的比较。

不同观点：
• **Gemini模型的能力与实际表现**：[johnfn]认为Gemini模型在某些任务中表现不如Claude Opus 4，尤其是在处理复杂的TypeScript问题时，Gemini显得笨拙，甚至会放弃任务。而Opus 4能更轻松地解决相同问题，且更具创造性。不过[johnfn]也承认Gemini仍然是一个不错的模型，只是Opus 4在他看来更胜一筹。

• **市场竞争与OpenAI的未来**：[chollida1]对OpenAI的未来表示担忧，指出随着Google和Facebook等公司加入竞争，OpenAI可能不再处于领先地位。此外，OpenAI的营收与高估值不匹配，未来在筹集资金和获取专有数据方面可能面临挑战，这可能影响其市场地位和估值。

主要讨论点：神经形态计算的技术、伦理及其发展前景

不同观点：
• [技术细节质疑] datameta 指出在描述功率时存在单位不匹配的问题，质疑“20瓦电力与两个LED灯泡24小时用电量”的类比是否准确。
• [伦理问题] kokanee 提出两个伦理问题：1) 如果人工大脑技术发展到极致，是否会与奴隶没有区别？2) 生物工程的真实人脑与功能相同的数字版本是否有伦理差异？
• [技术发展前景] geeunits 分享了自己在神经形态内核和操作系统方面的项目经验，并对未来硬件和软件范式转变持乐观态度，认为未来软件将对大多数人透明。
• [公司评价] stefanv 认为Numenta公司及其智能理论被低估，暗示其在神经形态计算领域有潜力。
• [现实挑战] Footpost 指出神经形态计算被炒作多年但表现不佳，尤其与当前的深度学习硬件如Google Edge TPU相比，其能效和训练成本不占优势。此外，目前科学对大脑如何产生智能的理解不足，因此模仿大脑机制可能为时过早。引用了Nvidia首席科学家的比喻来支持这一观点。

• [历史背景] ge96 提到“神经形态计算”这个术语至少有8年历史，暗示该领域并非新兴。
• [内容传播] newfocogi 对洛斯阿拉莫斯国家实验室（LANL）在Hacker News上突然增加的AI内容感到惊讶，质疑是内容发布策略的变化还是其他原因导致。
• [技术回顾] random3 简单提到忆阻器（memristors）再次受到关注，可能与神经形态计算相关。

• 神经形态计算的实际效能与伦理问题。Footpost与其他评论者对该技术的现实表现和前景存在分歧，同时kokanee提出了关于该技术伦理边界的深刻问题。

data.title: Cysteine depletion triggers adipose tissue thermogenesis and weight loss
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了限制卡路里摄入如何通过减少白色脂肪组织中的含硫氨基酸半胱氨酸，触发脂肪组织褐变和体重减轻。研究发现，小鼠中全身性半胱氨酸耗竭会导致致命性体重减轻，增加脂肪利用和脂肪细胞褐变，而恢复饮食中的半胱氨酸可逆转这些效果。机制上，半胱氨酸限制引发的脂肪褐变和体重减轻依赖于交感神经系统衍生的去甲肾上腺素信号，通过β3-肾上腺素能受体起作用，且与FGF21和UCP1无关。在肥胖小鼠中，半胱氨酸 deprivation 迅速引发脂肪褐变，增加能量消耗，导致30%的体重减轻并逆转代谢性炎症。这些发现表明，半胱氨酸在生物体代谢中至关重要，其去除可触发脂肪褐变和快速体重减轻。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕cysteine（半胱氨酸）与体重减轻的关系及其潜在应用的讨论

不同观点：
• riknos314：认为文章标题引导读者关注通过减少半胱氨酸来增加减重，但他更感兴趣的是，补充半胱氨酸可能有助于防止某些消耗性疾病中的过度体重减轻。他期待未来在这一领域有更多研究。
• jdnier：提供了2023年关于半胱氨酸和甘氨酸来源及其效果的研究综述链接，未直接发表个人观点，但引导读者查看相关资源。
• LPisGood：指出半胱氨酸是维持生命所需的重要蛋白质的基础组成部分，质疑将这些发现应用于人类减重或健身的潜在益处。
• biomcgary：解释半胱氨酸在氧化还原代谢和清除活性氧（ROS）中的关键作用，特别是在棕色脂肪燃烧过程中， deprivation of cysteine（剥夺半胱氨酸）可能产生特定代谢效果。
• drob518：个人关注是否服用NAC（N-乙酰半胱氨酸）会影响体重，提问停止服用NAC是否有助于减重。
• zajio1am：简短评论，提醒讨论的是小鼠实验，暗示可能不直接适用于人类。
• RS-232：提到半胱氨酸蛋白酶抑制剂可以减少细胞可用的游离半胱氨酸，并列举了一些天然来源，如木瓜、猕猴桃等。
• poirot2：幽默地提到胱氨酸尿症（cysteinuria）并不会导致体重减轻，暗示不同情况下半胱氨酸代谢可能有不同效果。
• jostmey：认为减少半胱氨酸作为减重手段过于极端，将其比作剥夺团队编写HTML的能力却期望代码运行更快，暗示这种方法可能过于激烈。
• readthenotes1：简短评论，提到“系统性半胱氨酸耗竭会导致小鼠致命性体重减轻”后表示没有继续阅读，暗示对该研究结果的怀疑。
• bilsbie：询问半胱氨酸与同型半胱氨酸（homocysteine）是否相同，显示出对两种物质区别的困惑。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于减少半胱氨酸是否可以作为有效的减重手段。一些人认为这可能是一种潜在的机制（如riknos314），而另一些人则认为这种方法过于极端且可能不适用于人类（如jostmey和LPisGood）。
- 实验结果主要基于小鼠研究，部分评论者提醒注意物种差异（如zajio1am）。
- 讨论还涉及NAC补充剂与体重变化的关系（如drob518），以及天然食物来源中的半胱氨酸调控（如RS-232）。
- 对半胱氨酸与其他类似物质（如同型半胱氨酸）的混淆也出现在评论中（如bilsbie），显示出对具体科学细节的进一步澄清需求。

44193225.article_content:
Cysteine depletion triggers adipose tissue thermogenesis and weight loss
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Fat metabolism
Homeostasis
Metabolism
Abstract
Caloric restriction and methionine restriction-driven enhanced lifespan and healthspan induces ‘browning’ of white adipose tissue, a metabolic response that increases heat production to defend core body temperature. However, how specific dietary amino acids control adipose thermogenesis is unknown. Here, we identified that weight loss induced by caloric restriction in humans reduces thiol-containing sulfur amino acid cysteine in white adipose tissue. Systemic cysteine depletion in mice causes lethal weight loss with increased fat utilization and browning of adipocytes that is rescued upon restoration of cysteine in diet. Mechanistically, cysteine-restriction-induced adipose browning and weight loss requires sympathetic nervous system-derived noradrenaline signalling via β3-adrenergic-receptors that is independent of FGF21 and UCP1. In obese mice, cysteine deprivation induced rapid adipose browning, increased energy expenditure leading to 30% weight loss and reversed metabolic inflammation. These findings establish that cysteine is essential for organismal metabolism as removal of cysteine in the host triggers adipose browning and rapid weight loss.

44193225.article_summary: 本文探讨了限制卡路里摄入如何通过减少白色脂肪组织中的含硫氨基酸半胱氨酸，触发脂肪组织褐变和体重减轻。研究发现，小鼠中全身性半胱氨酸耗竭会导致致命性体重减轻，增加脂肪利用和脂肪细胞褐变，而恢复饮食中的半胱氨酸可逆转这些效果。机制上，半胱氨酸限制引发的脂肪褐变和体重减轻依赖于交感神经系统衍生的去甲肾上腺素信号，通过β3-肾上腺素能受体起作用，且与FGF21和UCP1无关。在肥胖小鼠中，半胱氨酸 deprivation 迅速引发脂肪褐变，增加能量消耗，导致30%的体重减轻并逆转代谢性炎症。这些发现表明，半胱氨酸在生物体代谢中至关重要，其去除可触发脂肪褐变和快速体重减轻。
44193225.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕cysteine（半胱氨酸）与体重减轻的关系及其潜在应用的讨论

不同观点：
• riknos314：认为文章标题引导读者关注通过减少半胱氨酸来增加减重，但他更感兴趣的是，补充半胱氨酸可能有助于防止某些消耗性疾病中的过度体重减轻。他期待未来在这一领域有更多研究。
• jdnier：提供了2023年关于半胱氨酸和甘氨酸来源及其效果的研究综述链接，未直接发表个人观点，但引导读者查看相关资源。
• LPisGood：指出半胱氨酸是维持生命所需的重要蛋白质的基础组成部分，质疑将这些发现应用于人类减重或健身的潜在益处。
• biomcgary：解释半胱氨酸在氧化还原代谢和清除活性氧（ROS）中的关键作用，特别是在棕色脂肪燃烧过程中， deprivation of cysteine（剥夺半胱氨酸）可能产生特定代谢效果。
• drob518：个人关注是否服用NAC（N-乙酰半胱氨酸）会影响体重，提问停止服用NAC是否有助于减重。
• zajio1am：简短评论，提醒讨论的是小鼠实验，暗示可能不直接适用于人类。
• RS-232：提到半胱氨酸蛋白酶抑制剂可以减少细胞可用的游离半胱氨酸，并列举了一些天然来源，如木瓜、猕猴桃等。
• poirot2：幽默地提到胱氨酸尿症（cysteinuria）并不会导致体重减轻，暗示不同情况下半胱氨酸代谢可能有不同效果。
• jostmey：认为减少半胱氨酸作为减重手段过于极端，将其比作剥夺团队编写HTML的能力却期望代码运行更快，暗示这种方法可能过于激烈。
• readthenotes1：简短评论，提到“系统性半胱氨酸耗竭会导致小鼠致命性体重减轻”后表示没有继续阅读，暗示对该研究结果的怀疑。
• bilsbie：询问半胱氨酸与同型半胱氨酸（homocysteine）是否相同，显示出对两种物质区别的困惑。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于减少半胱氨酸是否可以作为有效的减重手段。一些人认为这可能是一种潜在的机制（如riknos314），而另一些人则认为这种方法过于极端且可能不适用于人类（如jostmey和LPisGood）。
- 实验结果主要基于小鼠研究，部分评论者提醒注意物种差异（如zajio1am）。
- 讨论还涉及NAC补充剂与体重变化的关系（如drob518），以及天然食物来源中的半胱氨酸调控（如RS-232）。
- 对半胱氨酸与其他类似物质（如同型半胱氨酸）的混淆也出现在评论中（如bilsbie），显示出对具体科学细节的进一步澄清需求。

Millions in west do not know they have aggressive fatty liver disease, study says
Research finds more than 15m in US, UK, Germany and France with MASH have not been diagnosed
Anna Bawden
Health and social affairs correspondent
Thu 5 Jun 2025 07.50 EDT
Last modified on Thu 5 Jun 2025 15.04 EDT
Share
More than 15 million people in the US, UK,
Germany
and France do not know they have the most aggressive form of fatty liver disease, according to research.
Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) – the formal name for non-alcoholic fatty liver disease – occurs in people who drink no or minimal amounts of alcohol whose liver contains more than 5% fat.
About two-thirds of patients with type 2 diabetes are thought to have the condition, which is also associated with obesity, heart and circulatory disease.
Approximately 5% of adults globally have the most aggressive form of MASLD. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) causes fibrosis (scarring) and can lead to cirrhosis and is linked to greater risk of cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease and liver cancer.
But the vast majority of people do not know they have the condition. An international group of researchers examined prevalence and diagnosis of aggressive fatty liver disease in the US, UK, Germany and
France
.
The researchers found that just under 3% of people in the UK, France and Germany, and 4% of those in the US have MASH, but diagnosis rates were below 18%. That means about 20 million people in the US, UK, Germany and France are living with MASH but only 2.5 million people have a diagnosis, leaving more than three-quarters – about 16.7 million people – unaware they have the condition.
The
report, published in the Lancet Regional Health Europe
and presented at the meeting of the global thinktank on
steatotic liver disease
in Barcelona, Spain, on Thursday, calls for a doubling in diagnosis rates from 2022 levels. Traditionally, MASH was diagnosed through biopsy, but now non-invasive methods such as blood tests, ultrasound and MRI scans can be used. As a result, everyone with type 2 diabetes; obesity combined with one or more other risk factors; and those with persistently high liver enzymes should be screened for MASH, the researchers conclude.
Dr Jeffrey Lazarus, the lead author of the paper and a professor of global health in New York and Barcelona, said: “Undiagnosed MASH costs economies billions of pounds in lost productivity and poor health. Unless diagnosis rates are doubled, alongside similar increases in treatment and care, direct health costs alone are predicted to triple over the next 20 years.”
Responding to the findings, Emmanouil Tsochatzis, a professor of hepatology at University College London and a consultant hepatologist at the Royal Free hospital, said: “More than 15 million people across the US and Europe have the deadliest form of fatty liver disease – and don’t know it. Without faster diagnosis and access to treatment, the human and economic toll will skyrocket.”
The research has also prompted renewed calls for weight loss jabs to be used to treat MASH.
Contraception warning over weight-loss drugs after dozens of pregnancies
Read more
Dr Paul Brennan, a co-author of the Lancet paper and a hepatologist at NHS Tayside, said: “GLP-1s (including Wegovy and Mounjaro) offer the potential to resynchronise our metabolism, by introducing feelings of satiety – fullness – and delaying the time the stomach takes to empty. These effects often result in reduced calorie intake, and improvements in how the liver handles nutrients as a result of weight loss, thus reducing scar tissue formation in the liver.”
Michael Betel, the president of the Fatty Liver Alliance, said: “Too many people living with type 2 diabetes or obesity are never tested for MASH until it’s too late. We need a huge increase in liver health assessments in patients living with these diseases, alongside lifestyle changes and for some, when appropriate, weight loss drugs to reduce blood sugar and appetite. While weight loss drugs weren’t created to treat liver disease,
trials
suggest they could benefit multiple metabolic-related conditions, and improve our liver health.”
Separately a
study
published on Wednesday found that the diabetes drug dapagliflozin, which reduces blood sugar levels, can also reduce fat levels and fibrosis in the liver.

data.title: Eleven v3
data.author: robertvc
data.article_summary: ElevenLabs推出了Eleven v3（alpha），这是一款极具表现力的文本到语音（Text to Speech）模型。该模型支持通过音频标签控制情感、传递方式和方向，能够生成具有情感层次和丰富表现力的语音。它还支持多说话者动态对话，使生成的对话更加自然和人性化。Eleven v3涵盖70多种语言，提供全球受众可理解的精确语音表达。目前，该模型处于alpha阶段，自助用户在2025年6月底前可享受80%的折扣。API接口即将推出，更多音频标签和语言支持细节可查阅相关指南。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Eleven Labs的文本到语音（TTS）技术及其相关特性、质量和应用

不同观点：
• BalinKing认为系统在某些情况下会跳过特定的句子（如日语示例），虽然后来修复了，但这让人感觉像是窥见了系统背后的运作逻辑。
• Riebschlager提到该系统能够演唱歌曲，并提供了示例链接，展示了不同方式下生成演唱语音的效果，但某些流行歌曲未能触发演唱功能。
• Ianbicking对比了OpenAI的模型与Eleven Labs，指出Eleven Labs在音色变化上较为有限，但价格更便宜，同时指出OpenAI模型的音质和可预测性较低。
• Ricketycricket担心机器生成过于脚本化的语言会让人感到被 patronized（居高临下的对待），尤其是在寻求帮助时。
• P1necone认为生成的音频像广播广告中的语音，不自然，可能是因为训练集中此类数据过多或目标如此。
• Zamadatix指出美式英语语音表现很好，但在插入笑声时仍显生硬，像是一个专门的笑声部分，而非自然融入语音中的笑声。
• Palisade提供了技术来源信息，指出Eleven Labs基于的开源技术及其开发者的雇佣背景。
• Wewewedxfgdf提到没有看到英式口音的示例，且通常TTS系统的美式口音较好，而英式口音常显得不自然。
• RomanPushkin认为俄语的质量很差，质疑为何要加入不可用的语言选项。
• Artninja1988对系统的声音质量表示高度赞赏，认为几乎与专业配音演员无异，但关注其定价。
• Drag0s指出英语语音表现很好，但其他语言带有强烈的英语口音。
• Protocolture对系统中的“语音槽位”限制表示不满，但表示可以通过删除不需要的语音来解决。
• Flakiness认为日语语音比第二版有所改进，但仍不够自然，不建议用于广告等关键用途。
• Gosub100质疑是否可以购买该产品并训练自己的开源TTS系统，以及公司是否具备阻止此类操作的理由。
• Vwkd指出ElevenReader经常在数字上出错，例如将年份读错，这是一个需要仔细校对才能发现的细微错误。

补充讨论：
• 系统在不同语言和口音上的表现存在差异，尤其是非英语语言和特定口音（如英式、俄式、日式）的表现较弱。
• 对于系统生成语音的自然度和脚本化问题存在一定争议，部分用户担心其在实际应用中的表现，尤其是在需要自然语音交互的场景中。
• 价格和系统限制（如语音槽位）也是用户关注的重点，部分用户对系统的使用成本和灵活性提出质疑。
• 技术来源和开源问题也引发了讨论，用户对技术背后的开发背景和法律限制表示关注。

44194521.article_summary: ElevenLabs推出了Eleven v3（alpha），这是一款极具表现力的文本到语音（Text to Speech）模型。该模型支持通过音频标签控制情感、传递方式和方向，能够生成具有情感层次和丰富表现力的语音。它还支持多说话者动态对话，使生成的对话更加自然和人性化。Eleven v3涵盖70多种语言，提供全球受众可理解的精确语音表达。目前，该模型处于alpha阶段，自助用户在2025年6月底前可享受80%的折扣。API接口即将推出，更多音频标签和语言支持细节可查阅相关指南。
44194521.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Eleven Labs的文本到语音（TTS）技术及其相关特性、质量和应用

不同观点：
• BalinKing认为系统在某些情况下会跳过特定的句子（如日语示例），虽然后来修复了，但这让人感觉像是窥见了系统背后的运作逻辑。
• Riebschlager提到该系统能够演唱歌曲，并提供了示例链接，展示了不同方式下生成演唱语音的效果，但某些流行歌曲未能触发演唱功能。
• Ianbicking对比了OpenAI的模型与Eleven Labs，指出Eleven Labs在音色变化上较为有限，但价格更便宜，同时指出OpenAI模型的音质和可预测性较低。
• Ricketycricket担心机器生成过于脚本化的语言会让人感到被 patronized（居高临下的对待），尤其是在寻求帮助时。
• P1necone认为生成的音频像广播广告中的语音，不自然，可能是因为训练集中此类数据过多或目标如此。
• Zamadatix指出美式英语语音表现很好，但在插入笑声时仍显生硬，像是一个专门的笑声部分，而非自然融入语音中的笑声。
• Palisade提供了技术来源信息，指出Eleven Labs基于的开源技术及其开发者的雇佣背景。
• Wewewedxfgdf提到没有看到英式口音的示例，且通常TTS系统的美式口音较好，而英式口音常显得不自然。
• RomanPushkin认为俄语的质量很差，质疑为何要加入不可用的语言选项。
• Artninja1988对系统的声音质量表示高度赞赏，认为几乎与专业配音演员无异，但关注其定价。
• Drag0s指出英语语音表现很好，但其他语言带有强烈的英语口音。
• Protocolture对系统中的“语音槽位”限制表示不满，但表示可以通过删除不需要的语音来解决。
• Flakiness认为日语语音比第二版有所改进，但仍不够自然，不建议用于广告等关键用途。
• Gosub100质疑是否可以购买该产品并训练自己的开源TTS系统，以及公司是否具备阻止此类操作的理由。
• Vwkd指出ElevenReader经常在数字上出错，例如将年份读错，这是一个需要仔细校对才能发现的细微错误。

补充讨论：
• 系统在不同语言和口音上的表现存在差异，尤其是非英语语言和特定口音（如英式、俄式、日式）的表现较弱。
• 对于系统生成语音的自然度和脚本化问题存在一定争议，部分用户担心其在实际应用中的表现，尤其是在需要自然语音交互的场景中。
• 价格和系统限制（如语音槽位）也是用户关注的重点，部分用户对系统的使用成本和灵活性提出质疑。
• 技术来源和开源问题也引发了讨论，用户对技术背后的开发背景和法律限制表示关注。

data.title: IRS Direct File on GitHub
data.author: nickthegreek
data.article_summary: 2025年5月30日，美国国税局（IRS）已在GitHub上公开了其Direct File项目的绝大多数代码，作为开放源代码软件。由于Direct File是美国政府的工作成果，属于公共领域。此举提前三周 fulfilling 了SHARE IT Act的法定义务，展示了IRS建立公众信任和允许独立评估其工作的承诺。开放源代码不仅是为了透明度，更是为了确保纳税人能充分享受其应得的税收优惠。Direct File团队一直致力于通过准确、便捷和安全的报税选项来赢得公众信任。文章还提到，作者本人两周前已离开IRS，文中所述仅代表个人观点。代码可在GitHub上的IRS-Public/direct-file仓库中查看。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IRS公开Direct File项目的源代码及其相关问题

不同观点：
• hydrogen7800认为，虽然源代码公开了，但与收入系统互操作性和对现行税法的遵守才是关键，这些部分仍可能被政府阻止。
• 90s_dev关注代码的技术实现，特别是使用Java语言的部分，并提出了关于其常见性的问题。
• pimlottc指出除了代码外，还有许多设计文档和流程图值得关注，但这些文件无法在线直接查看。
• ronbenton对项目被现任政府取消表示遗憾，特别提到了团队的努力和项目的潜力。
• timhigins对被豁免的代码部分表示好奇，尤其是哪些功能被移除或重写。
• Zambyte质疑为何要创建新的IRS-Public小组而不是使用现有的irsgov小组。
• timerol提到关于子模块指针的错误，以及由于法律原因需要特别声明代码为公共领域。
• elif认为当前系统过于依赖个人主观判断，建议由权威机构客观决定税款，并建立上诉流程。
• bigon对美国国税局不提供免费报税平台表示疑惑。
• adamdecaf分析了项目中使用的多种编程语言，并强调了其多样性。

补充讨论：
• jsmovage和jsmo只是简单地对项目链接和分享表示感谢，未深入讨论技术问题。
• divbzero提到了上周相关讨论的链接，指向一个更广泛的讨论（62条评论）。
• tomhow提供了一个关于“告别”的文章链接，可能暗示对项目结束的情感反应。

争议焦点：
• 项目虽然公开了源代码，但其实际执行和与税务系统的整合仍可能受到政府限制（hydrogen7800的观点）。
• 项目的取消是否合理，尤其是考虑到团队的努力和项目的潜力（ronbenton的观点）。
• 当前报税系统是否应减少对个人判断的依赖，改为由权威决定并通知税款（elif的观点）。

44182356.article_content:
Direct File on GitHub
Friday, May 30, 2025
The IRS has now published
the vast majority of Direct File’s code on GitHub
as open-source software. As a work of the U.S. government, Direct File is in the public domain. And now everyone can check it out.
Releasing Direct File’s source code demonstrates that the IRS is fulfilling its obligations under the
SHARE IT Act
(three weeks ahead of schedule!). Now that Direct File has paved the way, I hope that more of the IRS’s code, paid for with taxpayer dollars, will soon be available to all of us.
Open sourcing Direct File has long been planned, and even longer desired. Explaining last May why open source is particularly important for Direct File,
the team wrote
:
The IRS could take further steps to build public trust and enable independent assessment of its work. The Direct File product team was given the mandate to develop software that ensures every taxpayer receives the full benefit of any tax provisions for which they are eligible. Releasing components of Direct File as open-source software would enable the team to demonstrate this commitment.
Establishing trust with taxpayers was core to our approach for designing and building Direct File. By creating the most accurate option for filing, by making taxes accessible to all, by keeping taxpayer data secure, and now, by publicly sharing Direct File’s code, the Direct File team showed our dedication to earning taxpayers’ trust.
Please note: As of two weeks ago, I no longer work at the IRS. I am writing solely in my personal capacity.
https://github.com/IRS-Public/direct-file

data.title: Statement on California State Senate Advancing Dangerous Surveillance Bill
data.author: noptd
data.article_summary: 多个组织（包括电子前沿基金会、TechEquity、加州消费者联合会等）联合声明，反对加州参议院通过的S.B. 690法案。他们警告，该法案可能导致科技公司监视民众，获取敏感个人信息，如移民身份和医疗记录。法案未限制公司如何使用或分享这些信息，可能将其提供给数据中介、移民局或限制生殖和性别确认护理的州的执法部门。在联邦机构基于收集的政治信仰、宗教 affiliations或健康决策针对个人时，通过该法案将增加敏感信息泄露风险。声明呼吁立法机构保护加州民众隐私，而非让联邦政府更容易获取敏感信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于先前讨论主题的延伸讨论，涉及技术社区中的文化现象、技术决策的影响以及开源项目的治理问题。

不同观点：
• **观点一**：一些用户认为技术社区中的决策往往受到个人偏好和流行趋势的影响，而不是基于技术本身的优劣。例如，某些编程语言或工具的流行可能并不完全与其技术优势相匹配，而是因为某些意见领袖或大公司的推广。[例子：有人提到Python的流行更多是因为Google的使用，而不是其技术优越性。]

• **观点二**：另一种看法是，技术社区的决策是集体智慧的体现，流行趋势反映了许多人的实际需求和使用体验。社区的反馈和迭代过程有助于筛选出最适合广泛使用的工具和技术。[反驳例子：开源项目的广泛使用和社区支持往往是其质量和实用性的证明。]

• **观点三**：有讨论提到开源项目的治理问题，认为项目领导者在做出决策时应更加透明和民主，充分考虑社区的意见。这有助于避免个人偏见对项目发展的负面影响。[例子：一些大型开源项目如Python通过治理委员会来平衡各方利益。]

• **观点四**：还有人指出，技术社区的文化现象有时会导致“回声室效应”，即社区内部的观点和偏好被不断强化，而外部的声音和不同的意见被忽视。这种现象可能会限制技术的多样性和创新性。[例子：某些技术社区对新技术的排斥和对旧技术的固守。]

补充讨论：
• 一些评论探讨了技术教育的重要性，认为教育机构和培训项目应注重培养学生的独立思考能力，而不是仅仅传授当前流行的技术。[例子：强调学习计算机科学基础知识的重要性，而不仅仅是追逐热门编程语言。]

• 争议的焦点在于技术决策过程中个人偏好与集体智慧之间的平衡，以及如何在开源项目中实现更加民主和有效的治理。这些争议反映了技术社区在快速发展过程中面临的挑战和机遇。

44194118.article_content:
In the wake of the California State Senate’s passage of S.B. 690, the
Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF)
,
TechEquity
,
Consumer Federation of California
,
Tech Oversight California
,
ACLU California Action
,
Privacy Rights Clearinghouse
, and the
California Low Income Consumers Coalition
issued a joint statement warning that the bill would put the safety and privacy of millions of Californians at serious risk:
“SB 690 gives the green-light to dystopian big tech surveillance practices which will endanger the privacy and safety of all Californians. SB 690 would allow companies to spy on us to get our sensitive personal information, such as our immigration status or what healthcare we’ve received. And once they have our sensitive personal information, SB 690 places no limits on how that business can use or share that information, allowing them to share it with data brokers, immigration officials, or law enforcement officials in states that restrict reproductive or gender-affirming care.
“At a time where agencies of the federal government are actively targeting individuals based on information collected from businesses about their political beliefs, religious affiliations, or health decisions, we cannot risk sharing even more sensitive information with them. The legislature should be doing all it can to protect Californians, not make it easier for the federal government to secretly obtain our sensitive information.”
Update: This post has been updated to reflect additional signers.

• **观点一**：一些用户认为技术社区中的决策往往受到个人偏好和流行趋势的影响，而不是基于技术本身的优劣。例如，某些编程语言或工具的流行可能并不完全与其技术优势相匹配，而是因为某些意见领袖或大公司的推广。[例子：有人提到Python的流行更多是因为Google的使用，而不是其技术优越性。]

• **观点二**：另一种看法是，技术社区的决策是集体智慧的体现，流行趋势反映了许多人的实际需求和使用体验。社区的反馈和迭代过程有助于筛选出最适合广泛使用的工具和技术。[反驳例子：开源项目的广泛使用和社区支持往往是其质量和实用性的证明。]

• **观点三**：有讨论提到开源项目的治理问题，认为项目领导者在做出决策时应更加透明和民主，充分考虑社区的意见。这有助于避免个人偏见对项目发展的负面影响。[例子：一些大型开源项目如Python通过治理委员会来平衡各方利益。]

• **观点四**：还有人指出，技术社区的文化现象有时会导致“回声室效应”，即社区内部的观点和偏好被不断强化，而外部的声音和不同的意见被忽视。这种现象可能会限制技术的多样性和创新性。[例子：某些技术社区对新技术的排斥和对旧技术的固守。]

补充讨论：
• 一些评论探讨了技术教育的重要性，认为教育机构和培训项目应注重培养学生的独立思考能力，而不是仅仅传授当前流行的技术。[例子：强调学习计算机科学基础知识的重要性，而不仅仅是追逐热门编程语言。]

• 争议的焦点在于技术决策过程中个人偏好与集体智慧之间的平衡，以及如何在开源项目中实现更加民主和有效的治理。这些争议反映了技术社区在快速发展过程中面临的挑战和机遇。

data.title: I Think I'm Done Thinking About GenAI for Now
data.author: cratermoon
data.article_summary:
文章的作者是一位自认为善于思考的程序员，他最初自比为像福尔摩斯一样的天才，通过系统观察做出敏锐推断。然而，他逐渐意识到自己更像电视角色Monk——虽然神经质且受困于心理问题，但能通过关注细节和解决 incongruity（不协调之处）来破解案件。作者通常通过反复思考和调整，将复杂想法理顺并写出文字或开发软件，从而使大脑平静下来。

然而，在面对生成式AI（genAI）时，作者发现自己无法理顺相关的不协调感，尽管他接触到大量相关讨论。他感到这些讨论无休无止、令人疲惫，且无法构建出令人信服的观点。他撰写此文并非为了说服他人，而是为了整理自己的想法并表达负面感受，以停止重复思考这一问题。

作者批评了一些"反反genAI"的文章，认为它们未能触及严肃批评的实质内容，而是通过回避具体来源和论点来简化问题。最终，他希望通过此文让自己和有类似困扰的人能够摆脱这一令人疲惫的讨论。

Like many other self-styled thinky programmer guys, I like to imagine myself as
a sort of
Holmesian
genius,
making trenchant observations, collecting them, and then synergizing them into
brilliant deductions with the keen application of my powerful mind.
However, several years ago, I had an epiphany in my self-concept.  I finally
understood that, to the extent that I
am
usefully clever, it is less in a
Holmesian idiom, and more, shall we say,
Monkesque
.
For those unfamiliar with either of the respective franchises:
Holmes is a towering intellect honed by years of training, who catalogues
intentional, systematic observations and deduces logical, factual conclusions
from those observations.
Monk, on the other hand, while also a reasonably intelligent guy, is highly
neurotic, wracked by unresolved trauma and profound grief.  As both a
consulting job and a coping mechanism, he makes a habit of erratically
wandering into crime scenes, and, driven by a carefully managed jenga tower
of mental illnesses, leverages his dual inabilities to solve crimes.  First,
he is unable to filter out apparently inconsequential details, building up a
mental ratâs nest of trivia about the problem; second, he is unable to let go
of any minor incongruity, obsessively ruminating on the collection of facts
until they all make sense in a consistent timeline.
Perhaps surprisingly, this tendency serves both this fictional wretch of a
detective, and myself, reasonably well.  I find annoying incongruities in
abstractions and I fidget and fiddle with them until I end up building
something that
a lot of people like
, or perhaps
something that a smaller number of people get
really
excited
about
.  At worst, at least

.  This is a self-soothing
activity but it turns out that, managed properly, it can very effectively
soothe others as well.

out or fit into a logical framework to make sense.  I am, somewhat reluctantly,
a

skeptic
.  However, I am,
even more
reluctantly, exposed to genAI Discourse every damn minute of every damn day.
It is relentless, inescapable, and exhausting.

understand how I usually address problematical ideas by thinking and thinking
and fidgeting with them until I manage to write some words â or perhaps a new
open source package â that logically orders the ideas around it in a way which
allows my brain to calm down and let it go, and how that process is important
to me.
In this particular instance, however, genAI has defeated me.  I cannot make it
make sense, but I need to stop thinking about it anyway.  It is too much and I
need to give up.
My goal with this post is not to
convince
anyone of anything in particular â
and weâll get to why that is a bit later â but rather:
to set out my current understanding in one place, including all the various
negative feelings which are still bothering me, so I can stop repeating it
elsewhere,
to explain
why
I cannot build a case that I think
should
be particularly
convincing to anyone else, particularly to someone who actively disagrees
with me,
in so doing, to illustrate why I think the discourse is so fractious and
unresolvable, and finally
to give myself, and hopefully by proxy to give others in the same situation,
permission to just peace out of this nightmare quagmire corner of the
noosphere.
But first, just because I canât
prove
that my interlocutors are
Wrong On The
Internet
, doesnât mean I wonât explain why I
feel
like they are wrong.
The Anti-Antis
Most recently, at time of writing, there have been a spate of âthe genAI
discourse is badâ articles, almost exclusively written from the perspective of,
not
boosters
exactly, but pragmatically minded (albeit concerned) genAI
users, wishing for the skeptics to be more pointed and accurate in our
critiques.  This is anti-anti-genAI content.
I am not going to link to any of these, because, as part of their
self-fulfilling prophecy about the âgenAI discourseâ, theyâre
also
all bad.
Mostly, however, they had very little worthwhile to respond to because they
were straw-manning their erstwhile interlocutors.  They are all getting annoyed
at âbad genAI criticismâ while failing to engage with â and often failing to
even
mention
â most of the actual
substance
of any serious genAI
criticism.  At least, any of the criticism that Iâve personally read.

your own ideas.  So, I understand that they didnât link directly to particular

since thatâs exactly what this post is doing too.

data.title: AGI is not multimodal
data.author: danielmorozoff
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了生成型AI模型在实现人工通用智能（AGI）方面的局限性。尽管这些模型在某些任务上表现出色，但它们依赖于扩展硬件能力，而不是对智能问题的深思熟虑的解决方案。多模态方法看似提供了一条通向AGI的清晰路径，但实际上忽略了具身认知和与环境互动的重要性。真正的AGI需要对物理世界有实际理解，而不仅仅是对符号的操作。大语言模型（LLMs）通过预测下一个标记表现出类似人类的语言理解，但这只是表面现象，缺乏对现实的深层理解。文章强调，AGI必须能够解决源于物理现实的问题，如修理汽车或做饭，这需要将具身认知和环境互动视为核心，而非仅仅依赖模态处理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AGI（通用人工智能）的架构、实现方式及其局限性

不同观点：
• ryankrage77认为，AGI需要一种能够持续运行并“体验”时间流逝的架构，以更好地理解因果关系。当前的大语言模型（LLM）只是预测下一个token，这种方法缺乏对因果关系的深刻理解。语言本身是一个强大的工具，生成合理的语言不一定需要真正的智能。
• nsagent支持近期的一个趋势，引用了一些相关论文和访谈，认为需要更加理论化的方法来处理数据和训练，而不是单纯依赖计算资源。
• patrickscoleman指出，有些评论没有仔细阅读文章内容，建议使用更具描述性的标题来避免误解。
• xigency认为，AI研究往往由那些认为智力是全序的人主导，而智力实际上是部分有序的，不同的人在不同方面有各自的优势。
• itkovian_批评某些符号/具身认知的倡导者对大模型的理解不深，导致得出奇怪的结论。例如，某些人建议的设计实际上已经是当前普遍采用的方法。
• mountainriver认为，可以通过端到端的方式训练编码器，当前的分离处理是因为我们可以轻松缓存语言标记，而图像则不行。
• chrsw建议，先尝试构建像星鱼、蚂蚁或蠕虫这样简单的智能，再逐步提升复杂性。
• ineedasername指出，当前LLM方法已经颠覆了许多人之前对技术能力的预期，现在判断AGI的极限还为时过早。
• tolleydbg持怀疑态度，认为AGI并不真实。
• K0balt认为，具身经验是发展“真实”AGI的必要前提，人类很难识别不共享物理经验的智能。
• hardwaresofton将讨论与人类感官器官类比，认为AGI可能需要在一个模拟世界中训练。
• skybrian质疑“全域通用智能”的定义，指出没有任何人类拥有所有天赋。
• nexttk反驳“LLM仅仅是下一个token预测器”的观点，认为这种看法忽略了LLM的实际实现和能力，预测下一个token并不限制其思考和生成能力。
• fusionadvocate推荐Marvin Minsky的《The Society of Mind》一书，认为其中关于多模态系统的组织方法对理解该主题有帮助。

补充讨论：
• AGI是否需要具身经验和时间感知能力是一个重要争议点。
• 对当前LLM能力和局限性的不同看法，以及是否应超越“LLM是下一个token预测器”的简单描述。
• 对多模态输入和输出在AGI实现中的重要性有不同见解。
• 对智力是全序还是部分有序的讨论，反映了人们对智能本质的不同理解。

"In projecting language back as the model for thought, we lose sight of the tacit embodied understanding that undergirds our intelligence." –Terry Winograd
The recent successes of generative AI models have convinced some that AGI is imminent. While these models appear to capture the essence of human intelligence, they defy even our most basic intuitions about it. They have emerged not because they are thoughtful solutions to the problem of intelligence, but because they
scaled
effectively on
hardware we already had
. Seduced by the fruits of scale, some have come to believe that it provides a clear pathway to AGI. The most emblematic case of this is the multimodal approach, in which massive modular networks are optimized for an array of modalities that, taken together,
appear
general. However, I argue that this strategy is sure to fail in the near term; it will not lead to human-level AGI that can, e.g., perform sensorimotor reasoning, motion planning, and social coordination. Instead of trying to glue modalities together into a patchwork AGI,
we should pursue approaches to intelligence that treat embodiment and interaction with the environment as primary
, and see modality-centered processing as emergent phenomena.
Preface: Disembodied definitions of Artificial General Intelligence — emphasis on
general
— exclude crucial problem spaces that we should expect AGI to be able to solve.
A true AGI must be general across all domains.
Any
complete
definition must at least include the ability to solve problems that originate in physical reality, e.g. repairing a car, untying a knot, preparing food, etc. As I will discuss in the next section,
what is needed for these problems is a form of intelligence that is fundamentally situated in something like a physical world model
. For more discussion on this, look out for
Designing an Intelligence
. Edited by George Konidaris, MIT Press, forthcoming.
Why We Need the World, and How LLMs Pretend to Understand It
TLDR: I first argue that
true AGI needs a physical understanding of the world
, as many problems
cannot be converted into a problem of symbol manipulation
. It has been suggested by some that LLMs are learning a model of the world through next token prediction, but it is more likely that LLMs are learning bags of heuristics to predict tokens. This leaves them with a superficial understanding of reality and contributes to false impressions of their intelligence.
The most shocking result of the predict-next-token objective is that it yields AI models that reflect a deeply human-like understanding of the world, despite having never observed it like we have.
This result has
led to confusion
about what it means to
understand language
and even to
understand the world
— something we have long believed to be a prerequisite for language understanding.
One explanation for the capabilities of LLMs comes from
an emerging theory
suggesting that they induce models of the world through next-token prediction
. Proponents of this theory cite the prowess of SOTA LLMs on various benchmarks, the
convergence of large models to similar internal representations
, and their favorite rendition of the idea that “language mirrors the structure of reality,” a notion that has been espoused at least by Plato, Wittgenstein, Foucault, and Eco. While I’m generally in support of digging up esoteric texts for research inspiration, I’m worried that this metaphor has been taken too literally. Do LLMs really learn implicit models of the world? How could they otherwise be so proficient at language?
One source of evidence in favor of the LLM world modeling hypothesis is
the Othello paper
, wherein researchers were able to predict the board of an Othello game from the hidden states of a transformer model trained on sequences of
legal
moves
. However, there are
many
issues with generalizing these results to models of natural language. For one, whereas Othello moves can
provably
be used to deduce the full state of an Othello board,
we have no reason to believe that a complete picture of the physical world can be inferred by a linguistic description.
What sets the game of Othello apart from many tasks in the physical world is that
Othello fundamentally resides in the land of symbols, and is merely implemented using physical tokens to make it easier for humans to play.
A full game of Othello can be played with just pen and paper, but one can’t, e.g., sweep a floor, do dishes, or drive a car with just pen and paper. To solve such tasks, you need some physical conception of the world beyond what humans can merely
say
about it. Whether that conception of the world is encoded in a formal world model or, e.g., a value function is up for debate, but it is clear that
there are many problems in the physical world that
cannot
be
fully represented by a system of symbols
and solved with mere symbol manipulation.

• itkovian_批评某些符号/具身认知的倡导者对大模型的理解不深，导致得出奇怪的结论。例如，某些人建议的设计实际上已经是当前普遍采用的方法。
• mountainriver认为，可以通过端到端的方式训练编码器，当前的分离处理是因为我们可以轻松缓存语言标记，而图像则不行。
• chrsw建议，先尝试构建像星鱼、蚂蚁或蠕虫这样简单的智能，再逐步提升复杂性。
• ineedasername指出，当前LLM方法已经颠覆了许多人之前对技术能力的预期，现在判断AGI的极限还为时过早。
• tolleydbg持怀疑态度，认为AGI并不真实。
• K0balt认为，具身经验是发展“真实”AGI的必要前提，人类很难识别不共享物理经验的智能。
• hardwaresofton将讨论与人类感官器官类比，认为AGI可能需要在一个模拟世界中训练。
• skybrian质疑“全域通用智能”的定义，指出没有任何人类拥有所有天赋。
• nexttk反驳“LLM仅仅是下一个token预测器”的观点，认为这种看法忽略了LLM的实际实现和能力，预测下一个token并不限制其思考和生成能力。
• fusionadvocate推荐Marvin Minsky的《The Society of Mind》一书，认为其中关于多模态系统的组织方法对理解该主题有帮助。

补充讨论：
• AGI是否需要具身经验和时间感知能力是一个重要争议点。
• 对当前LLM能力和局限性的不同看法，以及是否应超越“LLM是下一个token预测器”的简单描述。
• 对多模态输入和输出在AGI实现中的重要性有不同见解。
• 对智力是全序还是部分有序的讨论，反映了人们对智能本质的不同理解。

data.title: Machine Code Isn't Scary
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了作者对机器码的认识过程，从最初认为低级语言和机器码很可怕，到后来通过学习发现机器码并不可怕。作者以ARM 64位指令集为例，介绍了机器码的三个基本概念：指令、寄存器和内存。指令是运行代码，以数字形式表示，每个指令都是32位数。寄存器是存储值的小地方，AArch64有31个通用寄存器。通过具体例子，作者解释了如何通过设置指令的不同部分来实现加法操作。文章还提到不同处理器有不同的指令集，如x86-64和ARM，并强调机器码实际上是一种数据结构，只要掌握其规律就不难理解。最后，作者建议使用简化的文本格式来代替直接编写二进制或十六进制数。

44177446.article_content:
Jimmy Miller
Machine Code Isn't Scary
The first programming language I ever learned was ActionScript. Writing code for Macromedia's Flash might be the furthest away from "bare metal" as you can possibly get. As I continued learning new languages, this starting heritage stuck with me. I was mostly interested in high-level, "web languages". Low-level languages felt impenetrable. Over time, I learned a bit more about them here and there, but for some reason, this notion stuck with me. Low-level things are scary, and machine code epitomized that most directly. When I Googled things asking about writing in "straight machine code", I was met with discouraging messages rather than learning.
Eventually, I decided I needed to overcome this barrier if I was going to achieve my goals. In doing so, I learned something I didn't expect.
Machine code isn't scary. If you can make sure your JSON conforms to a JSON schema, you can write machine code.
Which Machine Code?
One problem with machine code is that there isn't simply one standard. There are many different "instruction sets" depending on the processor. Most modern PCs use x86-64 machine code, but newer Macs, Raspberry Pis, and most mobile devices use ARM. There are other architectures out there, especially as you go back in time. The goal of this article won't be to give you a deep understanding of any particular instruction set, but instead, to give you enough information about how machine code typically works so you cannot be afraid of machine code. So we will start by having our examples be in ARM 64-bit (also written as aarch64). Once we have a decent understanding of that, we will talk a bit about x86-64.
Machine Code Basics
To understand the basics of machine code, you need three concepts:
Instructions
Registers
Memory
Instructions are exactly what they sound like; they are the code that will run. Machine code instructions are just numbers. In fact, in AArch64, every instruction is a 32-bit number. Instructions encode what operation the machine should run (add, move, subtract, jump, etc.) and accept some arguments for what data to operate on. These arguments might be constants (meaning like the number 2; these constants are often called "immediates"), but they can also be registers or a memory address. For now, just think of a register as a variable and memory as a list.

Here is an example of the instruction

Now this might look a bit confusing, but once you've seen these tables long enough, they start to be fairly straightforward. Each column in this table represents a single bit in a 32-bit number. If the value is a 0 or 1, that just means it is already filled in. If it has a label, it is a variable that needs to be filled in.
sf
tells us whether the registers we are going to use are 64-bit or 32-bit registers.
sh
stands for shift.

goes in conjunction with imm12, which stands for a 12-bit immediate (constant). So if we want to add

to something, we would put

in for

and set sh to 0 (meaning we aren't shifting the number). But what if we want to represent a number larger than 12 bits? Well, the add instruction doesn't let us represent all such numbers; but setting sh to 1 lets us shift our number by 12 bits. So for example we can represent
172032172032
by leaving our 42 alone and setting sh to 1. This is a clever technique for encoding larger numbers in a small space. Variables that start with R are registers, in this case, Rn is our argument to add, and Rd is our destination.
So the above instruction can be thought of like this:

Our add instruction is really just a data structure where we put the right parts in the right places.
Registers
Registers are small places to store values. Every instruction set will have a different number of these registers, different sizes of registers, different kinds of registers, and different naming conventions for registers. For AArch64, there are 31 general-purpose registers numbered X0 through X30 for 64-bit registers. Let's say we want to add 42 to register X0 and store the result in X1; we use this binary number.

. Registers are simply places where we can store values. But by convention, registers can be used for different things. These are called calling conventions and they are how "higher" level languages like C encode function calls.
Writing out all these binary numbers all the time (or even converting them to hex) can often be tedious. So instead, we usually talk about instructions in a simple text format

data.title: Cockatoos have learned to operate drinking fountains in Australia
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Cockatoos（凤头鹦鹉）及其他鸟类智力、行为特点的讨论，特别是它们操作饮水器等复杂行为的能力和动机。

不同观点：
• **Cockatoos的调皮和聪明**：[zik]认为凤头鹦鹉非常聪明且爱捣蛋，喜欢互相捉弄，也喜欢破坏东西。因此，它们学会操作饮水器并不令人意外。
• **个体差异**：[m463]分享了一个故事，说明即便是同种鹦鹉，个体之间也存在智力差异。故事中，雄性鹦鹉表现得更聪明，但当雌性鹦鹉被质疑时，它立刻展示了同样的能力。
• **左撇子现象**：[jen729w]提到一个有趣的现象，声称所有凤头鹦鹉都是左撇子，并通过观察大量鹦鹉吃东西的行为来支持这个观点。
• **饮水器行为的原因**：[haunter]对鹦鹉为何偏爱饮水器而非其他水源提出了两种假设：可能是因为饮水器的水更纯净，或者因为饮水器的高度有助于它们观察捕食者。
• **与其他鸟类的比较**：[srean]提到了Kea鹦鹉，并通过链接展示了Kea鹦鹉的认知能力，认为不同鸟类在智力上都有令人惊讶的表现。

补充讨论：
• **科学研究和证据**：[croemer]提供了关于凤头鹦鹉行为的原始研究链接，为讨论提供了科学依据。
• **鸟类智力的重新评估**：[Caelus9]认为像凤头鹦鹉和Kea这样的鸟类不断挑战我们对动物智力的认知，建议将“鸟类认知”作为一个独立的研究领域。
• **其他鸟类的行为趣闻**：[rconti]分享了关于Ibis（澳洲白鹮）的趣闻，描述了这种鸟在人类环境中的大胆行为，并通过幽默的方式讲述了自己与Ibis的对峙。
• **人类设施与鸟类行为**：[dottjt]提到了一则关于儿童将沙子带入饮水器的趣闻，说明了人类设施与动物行为的意外互动。
• **鸟类神经学研究**：[anjel]分享了一篇关于鸟类前脑神经元数量的研究文章，支持了鸟类具有较高智力的观点。
• **视频证据的稀缺性**：[fblp]对只有少量视频记录凤头鹦鹉操作饮水器的行为表示惊讶，并提供了一个相关视频链接。
• **对未来的幽默预测**：[dedicate]幽默地预测凤头鹦鹉可能会继续“征服”更多人类设施，甚至联想到了“猿猴星球”的情节。
• **推荐资源**：[metayrnc]推荐了一个展示这些鸟类解决问题能力的YouTube频道，为讨论提供了更多视觉资料。
• **更多鸟类恶作剧**：[ehnto]分享了更多关于凤头鹦鹉恶作剧的行为，包括从树上丢东西和干扰交通，还提到了一只无法飞行的救援Galah鹦鹉的聪明行为。
• **相关行为研究**：[_Algernon_]提到了关于蓝山雀偷牛奶的行为研究，为讨论鸟类复杂行为提供了另一个例子。

争议焦点：
- **个体智力的差异**：[m463]的故事表明即便是同种鸟类，个体之间也可能存在显著的智力差异，这与其他评论中对凤头鹦鹉整体智力的高评价形成对比。
- **鸟类智力的评估**：[Caelus9]提出鸟类认知能力可能被严重低估，这一观点引发了对传统动物智力评估方法的质疑。

总结：评论主要围绕凤头鹦鹉的聪明和调皮展开，讨论了它们操作饮水器等复杂行为的原因和动机，并通过个体故事、科学研究和与其他鸟类的比较，展示了鸟类智力的多样性和复杂性。

• **人类设施与鸟类行为**：[dottjt]提到了一则关于儿童将沙子带入饮水器的趣闻，说明了人类设施与动物行为的意外互动。
• **鸟类神经学研究**：[anjel]分享了一篇关于鸟类前脑神经元数量的研究文章，支持了鸟类具有较高智力的观点。
• **视频证据的稀缺性**：[fblp]对只有少量视频记录凤头鹦鹉操作饮水器的行为表示惊讶，并提供了一个相关视频链接。
• **对未来的幽默预测**：[dedicate]幽默地预测凤头鹦鹉可能会继续“征服”更多人类设施，甚至联想到了“猿猴星球”的情节。
• **推荐资源**：[metayrnc]推荐了一个展示这些鸟类解决问题能力的YouTube频道，为讨论提供了更多视觉资料。
• **更多鸟类恶作剧**：[ehnto]分享了更多关于凤头鹦鹉恶作剧的行为，包括从树上丢东西和干扰交通，还提到了一只无法飞行的救援Galah鹦鹉的聪明行为。
• **相关行为研究**：[_Algernon_]提到了关于蓝山雀偷牛奶的行为研究，为讨论鸟类复杂行为提供了另一个例子。

争议焦点：
- **个体智力的差异**：[m463]的故事表明即便是同种鸟类，个体之间也可能存在显著的智力差异，这与其他评论中对凤头鹦鹉整体智力的高评价形成对比。
- **鸟类智力的评估**：[Caelus9]提出鸟类认知能力可能被严重低估，这一观点引发了对传统动物智力评估方法的质疑。

总结：评论主要围绕凤头鹦鹉的聪明和调皮展开，讨论了它们操作饮水器等复杂行为的原因和动机，并通过个体故事、科学研究和与其他鸟类的比较，展示了鸟类智力的多样性和复杂性。

data.title: X changes its terms to bar training of AI models using its content
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: 社交平台X在其开发者协议中增加了一项限制，禁止第三方使用其内容来训练大型语言模型。更新后的协议明确规定，不得利用X的API或内容来微调或训练基础或前沿模型。这一变化发生在埃隆·马斯克的AI公司xAI于今年3月收购X之后，显然是不希望竞争对手免费使用其数据。此前，X在2023年曾修改隐私政策，允许使用公开数据训练AI模型，并在去年10月允许第三方训练模型。其他平台如Reddit和The Browser Company也已采取类似措施，防止AI爬虫未经授权使用其数据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用数据训练AI模型的合法性、道德性以及规则的讨论

不同观点：
• zombot：认为使用他人的数据训练AI是可以的，但自己的数据被盗用则不行，暗示双重标准。
• thih9：主张更严格的规则，建议需要内容作者的明确同意才能用于模型训练，或者要求模型的权重、提示和聊天记录与原始数据集具有相同的可见性。同时承认当前的规则不容易改变，但仍存在滥用的空间。
• lesuorac：质疑是否有人在对“Tweet”按钮文本进行AI训练，或者是否试图放弃第230条的保护以声称对网站上上传内容的 ownership。
• cameldrv：讽刺地表示Grok（一个AI）肯定会阅读每个被爬取网站的服务条款，并且不会使用禁止使用其内容的网站的数据。
• visarga：认为版权保护现状不佳，公司侵犯了数百万人在社交网络上发布内容的权利以及私人AI聊天的隐私。版权本应保护表达并保持思想的自由流通，但现在保护的是抽象内容，侵权变得更难确定。
• Animats：提出一个有趣的想法，即创建一个“经典AI模型”，该模型仅使用哈佛图书馆1926年以前的内容进行训练，这些内容已过版权期。
• blibble：希望能够修改自己的条款以禁止使用其内容训练AI模型。
• lcnmrn：表示在Subreply（一个社交网络）上允许所有机器人访问，并提供站点地图。
• kyle-rb：询问如果未签署X的开发者协议，是否可以使用下载的数据（如150k喜欢的推文）训练AI模型，特别是在用户协议中是否有条款禁止这种行为。
• delichon：引用X的服务条款，讨论在用户批准翻译的情况下，使用用户输入的URL（如推文）训练翻译模型的合法性问题。

补充讨论：
• bamboozled：对zombot的评论表示不满。
• michaelcampbell：简短地讽刺了“its content”的说法。
• seydor：建议对内容征收VAT，并认为所有用户应该获得报酬。
• petesergeant：认为唯一的新闻是xAI“收购”后花了2个月时间才采取行动。

争议焦点：
1. 使用数据训练AI模型的合法性和道德性，特别是未经明确同意的情况下。
2. 版权法的适用性和当前规则的不足，特别是在保护个人和公司之间的利益平衡方面。
3. 服务条款的解释和应用，特别是在涉及翻译模型和其他衍生用途时的边界问题。

这些观点反映了在AI技术快速发展的背景下，关于数据使用和版权保护的复杂性和多维度讨论。

44193390.article_content:
Social network X has changed its developer agreement to prevent third parties from using the platform’s content to train large language models.
In an update on Wednesday, the company added a line under “Reverse Engineering and other Restrictions,” a subsection of restrictions on use: “You shall not and you shall not attempt to (or allow others to) […] use the X API or X Content to fine-tune or train a foundation or frontier model,” it reads.
This change comes after Elon Musk’s AI company xAI acquired X in March — understandably, xAI wouldn’t want to give its competitors free access to the social platform’s data without a sale agreement.
In 2023, X changed its privacy policy to
use public data on its site to train AI models
. Last October, it made further changes to allow
third parties to train their models
.
Reddit has also put in place
safeguards against AI crawlers
, and last month, The Browser Company added
a similar clause
to its AI-focused browser Dia’s terms of use.
