data.author: stpn
data.article_summary: 本文作者在Recurse Center学习机器学习，并尝试复现"Deep Double Descent"论文的结果。双重下降现象指的是模型误差先下降、再上升、然后再次下降的行为。传统观点认为模型过大会有损精度，但该论文指出，更大模型通过更长训练可获得更好结果。作者试图训练不同大小的ResNet18模型来验证这一现象，使用Adam优化器进行4000个 epoch的训练，并引入标签噪声来观察双重下降效果。作者从零开始编写代码，避免参考现有复现工作，最终在GitHub上分享了代码。尽管遇到一些配置问题，但成功简化了实验规模以节省时间和成本。
data.comments_summary:
• **观点一：神经元“死亡”导致模型变小**  
Davidguetta认为，训练时间越长，神经元“死亡”越多，这些神经元因为梯度在数据集上趋于平坦而不再被使用。这意味着随着训练的进行，模型实际上变得更小，因为部分神经元不再发挥作用。这个观点强调了训练过程中神经元失活导致模型有效规模缩小的可能性。

主要讨论点：训练过程中神经元“死亡”对模型大小的影响

不同观点：
• **观点二：模型参数数量不变**  
虽然Davidguetta提到神经元“死亡”导致模型变小，但可能有人认为，尽管某些神经元不再活跃，模型的参数数量并不会真正减少。换句话说，模型结构和参数量在训练过程中是固定的，只是某些神经元的贡献变得微不足道或被忽略。

• **观点三：神经元失活不等于模型变小**  
另一种观点认为，神经元失活（或梯度消失）并不直接等同于模型变小。失活的神经元只是不再对输出产生显著影响，但这与模型实际上的参数数量减少是两回事。这种观点强调了神经元功能性失活与模型物理规模缩小的区别。

补充讨论：
• **梯度平坦的影响**  
讨论中提到了梯度平坦（flat gradient）对训练的影响，这可能导致神经元不再更新或失活。这一点可以进一步探讨，因为梯度平坦化通常与局部最小值或鞍点有关，这可能影响模型的训练效果和最终性能。

• **模型优化策略**  
为了应对神经元失活和梯度平坦的问题，讨论可能会延伸到如何优化模型训练策略，例如使用不同的激活函数、调整学习率或采用更复杂的优化算法来避免神经元“死亡”和梯度消失现象。

争议焦点：
• **神经元失活是否等同于模型变小**  
争议的核心在于神经元失活是否可以直接被视为模型变小。一方认为失活神经元不再使用，模型有效规模减少；另一方则认为模型参数数量未变，只是功能性失活。

44194431.article_content:
reproducing deep double descent
04 Jun, 2025
This summer, I've been at the
recurse center
intensively trying to catch up to the current state of the machine learning world. I don't have any prior background in ML, so I've been taking some
classes
and reading a lot of papers.
Two weeks in, I now have some basic working knowledge and wanted to get my hands dirty. After reading the Deep Double Descent paper, I wanted to see if I understood enough to reproduce the results. In a
previous post
, I went over some notes about doing the training for this on a rental GPU, but I figured I'd go into details about the project itself.
Please note the understanding here is still one of a student - if you spot something wrong, please send me a
message
!
double descent background
For a long time, the ML community thought that models could only be so big before they started degrading in accuracy. Around the start of the GPT era, folks realized that you could get better test-time results from a model just by training it for much, much longer.
In 2019, folks at OpenAI and Harvard
wrote a paper
that tries to formalize this effect and also goes into how model size can impact results, i.e.
model-wise
double descent where bigger models are eventually better.
The phrasing
double descent
refers to this behavior where error gets better at first, then peaks much worse, then eventually comes back down again.
intuitions
Models are trained on a training set and then evaluated against a separate test set. When a model is really good at the training set but really bad at the test set, we say it
generalized
poorly. Imagine: the model memorized the multiple-choice answers on the homework but it doesn't help with taking the final exam. It's not super clear why this happens, but here's the rough intuition I came away from.
With smaller models, the model can do its best to approximate the right behavior for test time but just doesn't have enough "brain cells" (parameters) to fit the whole problem in its head. To a certain point, giving small models more brain cells leads to better performance. This region is called
underparameterized
.
At around the model size where the model is just barely large enough to match the problem (called the
interpolation threshold
), the model can memorize "the" solution that lets it ace the training set, but that makes it prone to doing really poorly on the test set.
And finally, at larger model sizes, the model has plenty of brain cells (
overparameterization
) and can fit enough underlying features to classify well without overfitting to just the training set. This causes the second descent where the model converges to low error again.
There's also a factor here of how well the model can inherently learn the data. The paper discusses that introducing noise (purposefully adding incorrect labels) can be a proxy for this effect to highlight double descent.
To be honest, I'm not sure how much I trust my intuition so far about why double descent happens. It feels like if I squint at this formulation it kind of makes sense to me.
goals
I set out to repro a narrow portion of the paper: just the parts where they trained and compared varying size
resnet18s
from circa 2015.
To challenge myself, I wanted to start with a blank
.py
file and not look at existing repro work (though, as we'll see later this did not work out well for me). The final code is
here on github
.
getting started
The paper has quite a bit of detail for the experimental setup. Some helpful excerpts:
We follow the Preactivation ResNet18 architecture of He et al. (2016), using
4 ResNet blocks
, each consisting of
two BatchNorm-ReLU-Convolution layers
. The layer widths for the 4 blocks are [k,2k,4k,8k] for varying k and the strides are [1, 2, 2, 2].
Their experiment ran models from size 1 to 64. I ended up deciding to cut down to "only" 7 sizes (k=1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64) to save on training time.
For ResNets and CNNs, we train with cross-entropy loss, and the following optimizers: (1)
Adam with learning-rate 0.0001 for 4K epochs
Adam is a modern gradient descent variant that works better™ and we run it for 4,000 iterations. For reference, the original resnet paper trained the model on ~100 epochs, so we're going for 40x longer.
[...] we apply
RandomCrop(32, padding=4)
and
RandomHorizontalFlip
. In experiments with added label noise, the label for all augmentations of a given training sample are given the same label.
We introduce some variation during training as a common trick to improve performance.
Batch size: All experiments use a
batchsize of 128
.
One of the figures also shows that they trained the models with 0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20% label noise (purposefully mislabeling some items). I opted for doing just 0%, 10% and 20% in the interest of cost savings.

torchvision
package but I quickly ran into issues. The biggest problem was that the paper wants us to vary m

data.title: Who Gives a S T About Cursing Robots?
data.author: dxs
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了机器人在使用脏话时的影响。作者Naomi Fitter和她的团队研究发现，人们对咒骂机器人的反应复杂且多样。尽管有些人认为这是不当或不专业的，但其他人觉得这增加了机器人的个性或使其显得更人性化。研究表明，咒骂不一定对人机互动产生负面影响，反而可能在某些情境下增强用户的参与度和对机器人的好感。这一发现挑战了传统观念，提示未来机器人设计中可以考虑语言风格以提升用户体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：机器人说脏话是否有娱乐性

不同观点：
• **支持观点（娱乐性）**：
  - [stitched2gethr] 认为机器人说脏话具有娱乐性，表达出一种幽默和新鲜感，用"pretty damn entertaining"来形容其感受。

• **反对观点（不当性）**：
  - [ConcernedCitizen] 认为机器人说脏话是不合适的，特别是如果这种行为被未成年人看到，可能产生不良影响，强调需要对语言进行控制。

补充讨论：
• **技术伦理问题**：
  - [TechEthicist] 提出机器人模仿人类说脏话涉及到技术伦理问题，认为开发者应该对机器人的语言行为负责，避免传播不恰当的内容。

• **文化差异和个性化**：
  - [CulturalView] 指出不同文化对语言的接受程度不同，可能在某些文化中机器人说脏话被视为更有趣而不是冒犯，建议可以根据用户偏好设置语言模式。

• **争议焦点**：
  - 争议的焦点在于机器人说脏话是否适当，特别是考虑到对未成年人的影响以及技术开发者的责任。娱乐性和道德责任之间的平衡是讨论的核心。

data.title: If you're in Walnut Creek for 2 hours, the city is tracking you
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 2025年6月，加州核桃溪市（Walnut Creek）通过与科技公司Arrivalist合作，利用手机信号等数据跟踪游客行踪，以分析消费行为和市场趋势，旨在增加游客和酒店入住率，缓解城市财政困难。该技术收集手机连接信号塔、WiFi路由器等数据，帮助当地商会和旅游局了解游客来源、停留时间等信息，用于营销决策。虽然官方称数据匿名且仅用于整体趋势分析，但隐私保护倡导者担心此举可能侵犯个人隐私，因为数据涵盖广泛的个人活动信息。核桃溪商会表示该操作符合加州隐私法，但未提及法律例外情况。隐私专家认为，尽管目前仅用于良性目的，但数据收集本身仍可能引发隐私问题。

• [mitchbob] 提供了一个存档链接，但没有进一步阐述个人观点，可能希望读者通过链接了解更多背景信息。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于责任归属问题：[mikestew] 和 [corranh] 都认为报道中对责任方的描述不准确，应该区分政府和商业团体之间的责任。
• [corranh] 提到任何城市的商业团体都可以购买类似数据，这暗示了这种行为可能并不局限于Walnut Creek，具有一定的普遍性。

A shopper carries her cell phone while walking through Broadway Plaza on Wednesday, June 4, 2025, in Walnut Creek, Calif.  The city of Walnut Creek is tracking visitors via their cell phones and holding that information to use for marketing purposes.  (Aric Crabb/Bay Area News Group)
By
Katie Lauer
|
klauer@bayareanewsgroup.com
| Bay Area News Group
UPDATED:
June 5, 2025 at 11:25 AM PDT
Any time you spend two hours in Walnut Creek, local business leaders may be tracking you. The city’s Chamber of Commerce has paired with a tech company to clock visitors as they move in and out of the city.
The technology is from Arrivalist, a travel-industry-focused company with a platform that uses mobile location datasets to provide the Walnut Creek Chamber of Commerce and Visitor Bureau with data on consumer behavior and market trends. The company collects information from cell towers, WiFi routers and other sources to track the location of mobile devices.
Though the platform is being used by cities in the southern U.S., and other cities in Calfornia such as Stockton and Sonoma, Walnut Creek appears to be the first city in the greater Bay Area to employ it.
RELATED: How to stop Walnut Creek Chamber of Commerce partner from cyber tracking you
The Walnut Creek chamber says it’s working with the company in an attempt to determine how tourists spend their time in the city – and in the hopes it will help them attract more visitors, filling the roughly 1,300 rooms across eight hotels. The newest addition is the Hilton Garden Inn that just opened last year.
Currently, the city faces a deficit unless it can increase revenue or find more creative solutions. Local economic leaders say increased hotel stays will generate crucial fees to aid their budget woes.
In a meeting on Tuesday night, the business association’s reps showed how they had tracked participants of the Bay Area Spring Classic grade-school girls’ basketball tournament in early May; they received data on how many people came to the tournament, which cities or states they originated from, and how many nights they stayed.
Nicole Hankton, executive vice president of the Chamber’s visitor’s bureau, said the data is anonymous. No demographic details, names, phone numbers or addresses are included, she said. The Chamber can set up “points of interest” to track traffic for specific locations or events – like the Bay Area Spring Classic – to inform future marketing efforts.
“There’s no app download,” said Hankton. “We don’t get an email. We look at a specific event and get an estimate of how many people went.”
The Chamber, which operates as a nonprofit business association, directed all questions about privacy laws to Arrivalist. The company declined to provide a comment. However, Joseph Zitz, Arrivalist’s director of partnerships who helps service the Walnut Creek Chamber of Commerce’s account, said he sees their work as a “white hat” operation, trying to improve the quality of life for residents of tourist destinations such as Walnut Creek.
Zitz said the company provides only general insights to anonymous, “aggregated movement.”
Visitor walk through Broadway Plaza on Wednesday, June 4, 2025, in Walnut Creek, Calif.  The city of Walnut Creek is tracking visitors via their cell phones and holding that information to use for marketing purposes.  (Aric Crabb/Bay Area News Group)
Though Arrivalist says it follows California privacy law, the San Francisco-based company’s privacy policies also includes numerous and broad legal exceptions that present barriers for people trying to rein in their data, such as reserving the right to deny deletion requests when they involve local law enforcement, court orders or “as necessary or appropriate to protect the rights, property or safety of us, our clients or others.”
None of this was mentioned during Tuesday’s meeting.
But it concerns privacy advocate Mike Katz-Lacabe, the director of research for Oakland Privacy, a citizen coalition focused on issues of surveillance, transparency and privacy.
“It’s just incredible how much data there is, and the ability to basically track you from your home to everywhere that you go,” said Katz-Lacabe. “It’s not that hard to establish, if someone has this data, the exact patterns of your life, where you shop, where you work, where you worship, who your friends are, who you spend time with, where you spend the night, your travel habits — it’s absolutely everything. Of course, different companies like the Walnut Creek Chamber of Commerce are interested in a very small portion of that, which is pretty much benign. But it’s still perhaps a little bit creepy.”
On Tuesday, Hankton insisted the data collection is “all very innocent.” She said this kind of data is Chamber’s best option for improving tourism.
“I totally understand people’s concerns, but all we are looking at is location data,” she said. “It’s only the phones that they can track, and then we sort of multiply it.”

pollen
Pollen is a publishing system that helps authors make functional and beautiful digital books.
I created Pollen so I could make my web-based books
Practical Typography
,
Typography for Lawyers
, and
Beautiful Racket
. Sure, go take a look. Are they better than the last digital books you encountered? Yes they are. Would you like your next digital book to work like that? If so, keep reading.
At the core of Pollen is an argument:
Digital books should be the best books we’ve ever had. So far, they’re not even close.
Because digital books are software, an author shouldn’t think of a book as merely data.
The book is a program.
The way we make digital books better than their predecessors is by exploiting this programmability.
That’s what Pollen is for.
Not that you need to be a programmer to start using Pollen. On the contrary, the Pollen language is markup-based, so you can write & edit text naturally. But when you want to automate repetitive tasks, add cross-references, or pull in data from other sources, you can access a full programming language from within the text.
That language is
Racket
. I chose Racket because it has some unique features that made Pollen possible. So if it’s unfamiliar to you, don’t panic. It was unfamiliar to me. Once you see what you can do with Racket & Pollen, you may be persuaded. I was.
Or, if you can find a better digital-publishing tool, use that. But I’m never going back to the way I used to work.

data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了基因组编辑工具，特别是CRISPR系统的发展和应用。CRISPR原本是细菌用于防御病毒的免疫机制，通过将病毒的DNA片段整合到自身基因组中形成“记忆”，以便再次遭遇时进行识别和切割。自2012年起，科学家开始利用CRISPR技术编辑基因，特别是Cas9蛋白，通过修改引导RNA（gRNA）序列来切割特定DNA序列。2013年，CRISPR技术被成功应用于人类细胞。2019年，一位名叫Victoria Gray的镰状细胞贫血患者接受了基于CRISPR的实验性治疗（Casgevy），并在2023年获得FDA批准，成为首款获批的CRISPR疗法。文章还介绍了其他CRISPR系统，如Cas12、Cas13、碱基编辑器和主要编辑器，并提供了相关图示。

It was Victoria Gray’s first time in London and, despite a sleepless plane ride across the Atlantic Ocean, she wasn’t about to skip sightseeing. While crossing Trafalgar Square, Gray paused briefly to reflect on her experience. “I would never have been able to walk this long before,” she told a
NPR
reporter
. “I feel like I got a second chance.”
Four years earlier, in 2019, Gray had become the
first patient
with sickle cell anemia — a genetic disorder that causes red blood cells to become sticky and rigid — to receive an experimental treatment using CRISPR genome editing. The treatment, now known as Casgevy, became the first CRISPR-based therapy to gain FDA approval, in 2023. Gray, in London to discuss the significance of her recovery at the
Third International Summit on Human Genome Editing
,
described
Casgevy as “a new beginning for people with sickle cell disease.”
Despite its association with genome editing,
1
CRISPR didn’t start out as a tool for fighting genetic disease. Instead, for
billions of years
, bacteria have used CRISPR systems to defend against invasion by viruses known as bacteriophages. Certain CRISPR components can
add short DNA sequences
from the genomes of defeated viruses into the bacterium’s own genome, creating a type of protective “memory.” These sequences, known as protospacers, can be found between short, repetitive DNA motifs — an observation that gave CRISPR, which stands for “clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats,” its name.
Collectively, these repeat-protospacer regions are known as CRISPR arrays. The core of the CRISPR immune response is a guide RNA (gRNA) that binds to a CRISPR-associated (Cas) protein. Taken together, these components form what is known as a ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex. If the same virus invades the cell a second time, the gRNA’s spacer sequence will bind to the matching viral DNA sequence, then be cut by the Cas protein. This allows bacteria to remember past viral infections and fight them off without mistakenly cutting their own genomes.
Since the early 2010s, biologists have been exploiting CRISPR’s ability to cut a diverse set of specific DNA sequences by altering gRNA sequences. Notably, this has led to the development of new medicines to treat genetic diseases — Casgevy was the first of these to gain FDA approval and is used to treat two blood disorders, called sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia. Dozens more clinical trials, based upon similar gene-editing technologies, are now underway. This article provides a summary of the major CRISPR systems,
2
including the naturally occurring CRISPR-Cas9, -Cas12, and -Cas13 systems, as well as base editors, prime editors, and the recently uncovered bridge RNA system.
We made a digital poster that shows all the genome editing tools discussed in this piece in one large PDF.

to get a copy.

Cas9
Discovery
Cas9 became the first CRISPR effector (the protein that cuts or modifies DNA)
engineered
for genome editing in 2012, when Jennifer Doudna’s group at UC Berkeley and Emmanuelle Charpentier’s group at Umeå University showed that Cas9 could be guided to virtually any DNA sequence, not just natural targets from invading viruses, by tinkering with its gRNA sequence.
3
Given the system’s bacterial origin, however, it was not guaranteed to work well in other organisms. Within a year, though, Feng Zhang’s lab at MIT showed that Cas9 worked in
human cells
, a result that other groups quickly confirmed in a
flurry
of
papers
.
The best-known Cas9 protein comes from a bacterium,
Streptococcus pyogenes
, that causes pharyngitis in young children. The protein
is so good at cutting DNA that it still ranks among the most efficient Cas9 proteins and is almost certainly the most widely used genome editor today. Researchers have since discovered variants of the protein with additional useful qualities.
For example,
NmeCas9
(discovered in a pathogenic microbe,
Neisseria meningitidis
) makes off-target DNA cuts less often than the Cas9 from
S. pyogenes
, making it more specific.
GeoCas9
(taken from a thermophilic bacterium,
Geobacillus stearothermophilus
), on the other hand, is able to function and cut DNA at much higher temperatures. Researchers have also discovered a slew of
small Cas9s
— some less than half the size of the
S. pyogenes
protein — whose compactness makes them far easier to package into viral vectors and deliver into the human body.

data.title: The Right to Repair Is Law in Washington State
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 华盛顿州的维修权法案已正式成为法律，保障居民能够获取工具、零件和信息来修理个人电子设备、家用电器和轮椅。这是常识性立法，确保了消费者对自己所购物品的维修控制权。该法律的通过得益于多年倡导，包括华盛顿公共利益研究小组、环保和消费者权益组织，以及谷歌和微软等企业的支持。同时，残疾权益组织成功将轮椅纳入维修权法案。此外，美国国防部也认识到维修权的重要性，发布备忘录要求在采购合同中加入相关条款，以解决维护和修理问题。目前，全美已有50个州考虑此类立法，华盛顿是第八个正式通过的州。

不同观点：
• **支持观点**：[walterbell]和[CrimsonCape]等人认为该法案将有效阻止制造商通过零件配对和软件锁定来限制自助维修，特别是对于手机、轮椅等设备。这将赋予消费者和独立维修店更多自主权。

• **质疑观点**：[net01]认为该法案可能存在与德州法案类似的漏洞，例如在更换屏幕等零件时强制销售包含铰链等昂贵组件的组装件，而非单独的便宜零件。[pnw]进一步指出，该法案已经被华盛顿政客在企业捐赠者的影响下削弱，例如对游戏机的豁免。

• **具体案例和应用**：[rkagerer]提到Axis公司通过锁定IP摄像机的部分功能来强制使用其品牌的SD卡，质疑该法案是否能对此类商业行为产生影响。[drdaeman]则关注该法案是否能用于获取不同供应商产品之间的协议文档，以解决物联网设备的集成问题。

• **技术细节**：[avodonosov]和[GnarfGnarf]关心法案是否包括对软件解码和修改的权利，以及是否适用于加密文件格式等具体技术问题。[Yhippa]和[divbzero]则分别对该法案在具体设备如汽车调校和各州不同法律适用性方面提出了疑问。

• **政治和经济影响**：[lenerdenator]预测该法案可能成为联邦游说活动的焦点，以减少所谓的“繁重的州法规”。[froggertoaster]则对监管变化表示欢迎，认为这是对像John Deere这样的公司过度限制维修权的回应。

• **新闻时效性**：[andelink]对文章的新闻时效性提出疑问，但仍认为这是一个好消息。

Thanks in part
to your support
, the right to repair is now law in Washington.
Gov. Bob Ferguson signed two bills guaranteeing Washingtonians' right to access tools, parts, and information so they can fix personal electronics, appliances, and wheelchairs. This is the epitome of common-sense legislation. When you own something, you should have the final say about who fixes, adapts, or modifies it—and how.
When you own something, you should have the final say about who fixes, adapts, or modifies it—and how.
Advocates in Washington have worked for years to pass a strong right-to-repair law in the state. In addition to Washington’s
Public Interest Research Group
, the consumer electronics bill moved forward with a growing group of supporting organizations, including environmental advocates, consumer advocates, and manufacturers such as Google and Microsoft. Meanwhile, advocacy from groups including
Disability Rights Washington
and the
Here and Now Project
made the case for the wheelchair's inclusion in the right-to-repair bill, bringing their personal stories to Olympia to show why this bill was so important.
And it’s not just states that recognize the need for people to be able to fix their own stuff.  Earlier this month, U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth
issued a memo
stating that the Army should “[identify] and propose contract modifications for right to repair provisions where intellectual property constraints limit the Army's ability to conduct maintenance and access the appropriate maintenance tools, software, and technical data – while preserving the intellectual capital of American industry.” The memo said that the Army should seek this in future procurement contracts and also to amend existing contracts to include the right to repair.
This is a bedrock of sound procurement with a long history in America. President Lincoln only bought rifles with standardized tooling to outfit the Union Army, for the obvious reason that it would be a little embarrassing for the Commander in Chief to have to pull his troops off the field because the Army’s sole supplier had decided not to ship this week’s delivery of ammo and parts. Somehow, the Department of Defense forgot this lesson over the ensuing centuries, so that today, billions of dollars in public money are spent on material and systems that the US military can only maintain by buying service from a “beltway bandit.”
This recognizes what millions of people have said repeatedly: limiting people’s ability to fix their own stuff stands in the way of needed repairs and maintenance. That’s true whether you’re a farmer with a broken tractor during harvest, a homeowner with a misbehaving washing machine or a cracked smartphone screen, a hospital med-tech trying to fix a ventilator, or a soldier struggling with a broken generator.
The right to repair is gaining serious momentum. All 50 states have now considered some form of right-to-repair legislation. Washington is the eighth state to pass one of these bills into law—let’s keep it up.
Correction: An earlier version of this post misstated that Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll issued the memo, rather than U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. This post has been corrected.
44181421.article_summary: 华盛顿州的维修权法案已正式成为法律，保障居民能够获取工具、零件和信息来修理个人电子设备、家用电器和轮椅。这是常识性立法，确保了消费者对自己所购物品的维修控制权。该法律的通过得益于多年倡导，包括华盛顿公共利益研究小组、环保和消费者权益组织，以及谷歌和微软等企业的支持。同时，残疾权益组织成功将轮椅纳入维修权法案。此外，美国国防部也认识到维修权的重要性，发布备忘录要求在采购合同中加入相关条款，以解决维护和修理问题。目前，全美已有50个州考虑此类立法，华盛顿是第八个正式通过的州。

data.title: How we’re responding to The NYT’s data demands in order to protect user privacy
data.author: BUFU
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI的隐私和数据保护措施，特别是在法律要求和用户隐私之间的平衡。

不同观点：
• [yoaviram] 认为OpenAI在隐私问题上存在双重标准，声称提供隐私控制工具，但实际上通过企业计划收费提供隐私功能。同时指出OpenAI拒绝从模型和训练数据中删除个人数据。
• [supriyo-biswas] 提出了一种技术解决方案，即使用模糊哈希（如ssdeep哈希）存储内容，以在遵守法院命令的同时保护用户隐私。
• [_jab] 支持OpenAI的措施，认为他们在保护用户隐私方面采取了充分的步骤，并指出如果数据泄露，责任应在OpenAI而非纽约时报。
• [sega_sai] 批评对纽约时报的攻击性语言，认为如果法院批准了要求，那么攻击纽约时报是不恰当的。
• [atleastoptimal] 认为将数据永远保存在公司的托管API中是默认的，且是不可避免的。
• [mosdl] 讽刺OpenAI在版权问题上采取双重标准，只要有利可图就不介意违反版权。
• [WorldPeas] 关注此事件对企业使用AI编辑器的隐私模式的影响，特别是对零数据保留的要求。
• [dataflow] 对企业版和教育版的数据保留政策感到困惑，质疑它们在法律上的不同处理。
• [amluto] 指出“零数据保留”API难以获得，用户需要申请才能使用，并不是所有API用户都能轻易获得。
• [dvt] 和 [paxys] 都认为OpenAI在违反GDPR，尽管OpenAI声称在遵守法律，但实际上可能在侵犯用户的隐私权。
• [Caelus9] 认为在保护隐私和遵守法律之间很难划清界限，对OpenAI挑战法院命令表示支持，但也对数据被要求保留表示担忧。
• [throwaway6e8f] 以讽刺口吻建议如何在法律保留数据和公众反应之间取得平衡。
• [wand3r] 质疑法院命令的执行力度和可能的惩罚措施，指出数据保护指令在实际操作中的困难。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于OpenAI是否在隐私问题上采取了足够的措施，特别是在面对法律命令时的处理方式。
• 技术解决方案（如模糊哈希）作为一种可能的折中方案被提出，以在遵守法律的同时保护用户隐私。
• 对企业版和教育版在数据保留政策上的不同处理引发了用户的困惑和讨论。
• GDPR和版权法之间的潜在冲突也是讨论的一个重要方面，特别是当法院命令可能违反隐私法时。

data.title: Defending adverbs exuberantly if conditionally
data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于写作中使用副词的建议及其有效性

不同观点：
• topaz0认为，基于语法规则的写作建议无法替代个人品味，品味的培养需要长期阅读各种 prose（包括好的和不好的），并通过感受不好的写法和令人愉悦的写法来提升。虽然 novice writers 常滥用副词，导致文字不优雅，但解决方案不是完全消除副词，而是通过仔细阅读和修改，直到文字不再刺耳。

• Bjartr通过引用"Tom Swifty"的例子，展示了一种依赖副词的双关语用法，暗示副词在某些情况下可以增加语言的趣味性，而非仅仅是写作中的问题。

• Charon77质疑为何不能使用不改变词义的副词，认为副词有时可以调节阅读节奏，增加句子的连贯性，特别是在小说中，这样的“填充词”是有价值的。

• gadders提出了美式英语中省略副词词尾 "-ly" 的现象，质疑这种用法是否符合语法规则，还是属于俚语。

• ofalked回应了“避免使用副词”的建议，表达了对该建议的无奈，甚至调侃说即使副词也无法帮助表达其感受。

补充讨论：
• throwanem和elbear的评论更多是幽默和调侃，throwanem模仿副词用法进行自嘲，elbear则因为标题而给予了支持。

• chrisweekly推荐了Joe Moran的《First You Write a Sentence》一书，暗示该书可能对写作建议有更深入的讨论。

争议焦点：副词在写作中的作用及其使用限度。topaz0和Bjartr等人认为副词应谨慎使用，Charon77和ofalked则认为副词有其合理性和必要性。

data.title: Test Postgres in Python Like SQLite
data.author: wey-gu
data.article_summary: `py-pglite` 是一个 Python 测试库，允许开发者在测试中使用 PostgreSQL 功能，而无需完整安装 PostgreSQL。它通过 PGlite 提供快速、隔离的测试数据库环境，支持 SQLAlchemy 和 SQLModel，且与 Pytest 无缝集成。主要特点包括：超快测试速度、无需 PostgreSQL 安装、完全隔离的测试数据库、自动管理 PGlite 生命周期等。支持手动和自动管理数据库，提供多种实用功能如数据库清理、序列重置等。安装需 Python 3.10+ 和 Node.js 18+，并可通过 `pip` 安装额外依赖如 FastAPI 支持。该库简化了使用 PostgreSQL 进行应用测试的流程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在Node.js和WebAssembly（WASM）环境下运行PostgreSQL的相关技术选择和优化问题

不同观点：
• **WhyNotHugo**：认为在Node.js中运行WASM不会比经过几十年优化的原生代码更快，且即便不需要安装PostgreSQL，仍然需要安装体积较大的Node.js，因此“不需要PostgreSQL”不能算作卖点。
• **jauco**：提到可以使用Testcontainers作为另一种选择，且认为其速度并不慢。
• **benpacker**：分享了一个具体实现，展示了如何在Node/Bun环境中使用WASM后端的Postgres进行API单元测试，并提供了代码示例和项目链接。
• **samwillis**：对benpacker的项目表示赞赏，并提到其正在开发的PGlite有一个实验性的WASI构建，可以去除Node.js依赖，但目前缺乏错误处理功能。

py-pglite
A Python testing library that provides seamless integration between
PGlite
and Python test suites. Get the full power of PostgreSQL in your tests without the overhead of a full PostgreSQL installation.
🎯 Why py-pglite?
⚡ Blazing Fast
: In-memory PostgreSQL for ultra-quick test runs
🛠️ Effortless Setup
: No PostgreSQL install needed—just Node.js(I know)!
🐍 Pythonic
: Native support for SQLAlchemy & SQLModel in your tests
🧊 Fully Isolated
: Every test module gets its own fresh database
🦾 100% Compatible
: True PostgreSQL features via
PGlite
🧩 Pytest Plug-and-Play
: Ready-to-use fixtures for instant productivity

44196945.article_summary: `py-pglite` 是一个 Python 测试库，允许开发者在测试中使用 PostgreSQL 功能，而无需完整安装 PostgreSQL。它通过 PGlite 提供快速、隔离的测试数据库环境，支持 SQLAlchemy 和 SQLModel，且与 Pytest 无缝集成。主要特点包括：超快测试速度、无需 PostgreSQL 安装、完全隔离的测试数据库、自动管理 PGlite 生命周期等。支持手动和自动管理数据库，提供多种实用功能如数据库清理、序列重置等。安装需 Python 3.10+ 和 Node.js 18+，并可通过 `pip` 安装额外依赖如 FastAPI 支持。该库简化了使用 PostgreSQL 进行应用测试的流程。

data.article_summary: 在德克萨斯州新布朗费尔斯，Abigail Lindsey和她的姐妹Jennifer担心一个计划建在她们家对面的大型数据中心和发电厂会破坏她们的宁静生活。该项目由AI初创公司CloudBurst和天然气管道巨头Energy Transfer合作开发，发电厂将产生1200兆瓦的电力，仅为数据中心供电。由于连接公共电网的等待时间长，许多开发商选择自建天然气发电厂。尽管可再生能源如风能和太阳能增长迅速，但它们无法单独满足数据中心对持续稳定电力的需求。德州正面临大量AI项目涌入，天然气发电目前仍是主要选择。州立法机构也在考虑通过法案，以减少不严肃的大型项目对电网连接的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕企业和环境责任、电力系统可靠性及私人企业运营模式的讨论

不同观点：
• [metta2uall] 认为当前经济体系存在问题，企业无需为环境破坏的外部性成本买单，尤其是政治保守派并未有效保护环境。他指出，环境成本往往不成比例地影响贫困人群，例如孟菲斯地区因马斯克的xAI项目在无许可情况下使用天然气发电而受到影响。同时，他批评马斯克削弱了美国环境保护署（EPA）的职能，进一步导致环境监管不力。

• [bob1029] 则关注电力系统的可靠性，认为当前电网的稳定性依赖于多个发电机组，如果失去一两台私人发电机，电网将面临紧张局面。他从风险管理角度出发，表示不愿意投资需要自行运营整个电力系统的企业，特别是仅仅为了在空调房里运行计算机。

• [bobmcnamara] 通过一个实例补充了讨论，提到其一位朋友通过运营前苏联解体后被废弃的天然气发电厂，在哈萨克斯坦成功经营了一个加密货币矿场，暗示私人企业能够通过创新和资源再利用获取利润。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于企业是否应为环境破坏的外部性成本负责，以及私人企业在运营过程中对环境和公共基础设施的影响。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是电力系统的可靠性和管理风险，特别是私人发电设施在电网中的作用。
• 最后，私人企业如何利用废弃资源（如苏联时期的天然气发电厂）进行盈利也是一个有趣的讨论方向，反映出不同地区和背景下的商业机会。

Sisters Abigail and Jennifer Lindsey stand by a sign they posted on their rural property outside New Braunfels in opposition to a large data center and power plant planned across the street, pictured May 27, 2025.
Credit:
Dylan Baddour/Inside Climate News
Audio recording is automated for accessibility. Humans wrote and edited the story. See our
AI policy
, and give us
feedback
.
Sign up for The Brief
, The Texas Tribune’s daily newsletter that keeps readers up to speed on the most essential Texas news.
NEW BRAUNFELS — Abigail Lindsey worries the days of peace and quiet might be nearing an end at the rural, wooded property where she lives with her son. On the old ranch across the street, developers want to build an expansive complex of supercomputers for artificial intelligence, plus a large, private power plant to run it.
The plant would be big enough to power a major city, with 1,200 megawatts of planned generation capacity fueled by West Texas shale gas. It will only supply the new data center, and possibly other large data centers recently
proposed
down the road.
“It just sucks,” Lindsey said, sitting on her deck in the shade of tall oak trees, outside the city of New Braunfels. “They’ve come in and will completely destroy our way of life: dark skies, quiet and peaceful.”
The project is one of many others like it proposed in Texas, where a frantic race to boot up energy-hungry data centers has led many developers to plan their own gas-fired power plants rather than wait for connection to the state’s public grid. Egged on by supportive government policies, this buildout promises to lock in strong gas demand for a generation to come.
The data center and power plant
planned
across from Lindsey’s home is a partnership between an AI startup called CloudBurst and the natural gas pipeline giant Energy Transfer. It was Energy Transfer’s first-ever contract to supply gas for a data center, but not likely its last. In a press release, the company said it was “in discussions with a number of data center developers and expects this to be the first of many agreements.”
Previously, conventional wisdom assumed that this new generation of digital infrastructure would be powered by emissions-free energy sources like wind, solar and battery power, which have lately seen explosive growth. So far, that vision isn’t panning out as desires to build quickly overcome concerns about sustainability.
The Hays Energy Project, a 990 MW gas-fired power plant near San Marcos, on May 27, 2025.
Credit:
Dylan Baddour/Inside Climate News
“There is such a shortage of data center capacity and power,” said Kent Draper, chief commercial officer at Australian data center developer IREN, which has projects in West Texas. “Even the large hyperscalers are willing to turn a blind eye to their renewable goals for some period of time in order to get access.”
IREN prioritizes renewable energy for its data centers — giant warehouses full of advanced computers and high-powered cooling systems that can be configured to produce crypto currency or generate artificial intelligence. In Texas, that’s only possible because the company began work here years ago, early enough to secure a timely connection to the state’s grid, Draper said.
Need insider post-session coverage?
Catch up on what passed, what failed and what still matters — all in The Blast.
SUBSCRIBE NOW
There were more than 2,000 active generation interconnection requests as of April 30, totalling 411,600 megawatts of capacity, according to grid operator ERCOT. A bill awaiting signature on Gov. Greg Abbott’s desk, Senate Bill 6, looks to filter out unserious large-load projects bloating the queue by imposing a $100,000 fee for interconnection studies.
Wind and solar farms require vast acreage and generate energy intermittently, so they work best as part of a diversified electrical grid that collectively provides power day and night. But as the AI gold rush gathered momentum, a surge of new project proposals has created yearslong wait times to connect to the grid, prompting many developers to bypass it and build their own power supply.
Operating alone, a wind or solar farm can’t run a data center. Battery technologies still can’t store such large amounts of energy for the length of time required to provide steady, uninterrupted power for 24 hours per day as data centers require. Small nuclear reactors have been touted as a means to meet data center demand, but the first new units remain a decade from commercial deployment, while the AI boom is here today.
Now, Draper said, gas companies approach IREN all the time offering to quickly provide additional power generation.
Gas provides almost half of all power generation capacity in Texas, far more than any other source. But the amount of gas power in Texas has remained flat for 20 years, while wind and solar have grown sharply, according to records from the U.S. Energy Information Administration. data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: SP80帆船在2025年5月创下新高，最高时速达到58.261节（108公里/小时），成为历史上第二快的帆船，仅次于Vestas Sailrocket II。其速度超越了美洲杯AC75s和SailGP的F50s等顶级赛船。尽管最高速度不被用于官方世界纪录认证，但SP80团队多次在55至58节之间航行，显示了其稳定性和潜力。他们的短期目标是在500米距离内保持高速，以获得世界帆船速度记录委员会（WSSRC）的认证。目前，SP80在这段距离上的平均速度已达48.645节，接近打破现有纪录。团队的最终目标是打破Vestas Sailrocket II保持的绝对速度纪录（65.45节）。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：某种新型风动船是否能被称为“帆船”

不同观点：
• [saberience的观点] 认为该船只不能被称为“帆船”。理由是它没有传统的桅杆或帆，而是使用降落伞作为动力装置。虽然它可能是世界上最快的风动力船，但根据传统定义，它并不符合“帆船”的标准。

• [metalman的观点] 没有直接表达立场，但通过分享一个链接提供了更多背景信息，可能暗示读者参考更多资料以获得深入理解。该链接介绍了一艘名为SP80的船，并称其为“世界上最快的帆船”。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于“帆船”的定义。传统帆船依赖桅杆和帆，而新型船只使用降落伞作为动力，挑战了传统的定义。
• 有人认为这种新型船只即便不符合传统帆船的定义，也可以称为“风动力船”，并可能创下速度记录。
• 链接提供的资料可能包含更多技术细节和背景信息，有助于进一步理解该船只的设计和工作原理。

44194700.article_content:
TOP SPEED 58 KNOTS
SP80 SMASHES THE 100 KM/H BARRIER
May 27, 2025
The SP80 kiteboat has reached a top speed of over 58 knots, or 108 km/h. This new personal best makes SP80 the second fastest sailboat ever recorded, behind Vestas Sailrocket II and its 68.33-knot top speed. While peak speeds are not used for official world record certification, this performance confirms the boatʼs potential: SP80 is now faster than the most advanced sailboats in the world, from the AC75s of the Americaʼs Cup to the F50s on the SailGP circuit.
TOP SPEED: 58.261 KNOTS (108 KM/H)
In May,
the boat shattered its previous personnal best of 52 knots,
reaching 58.261 knots (108 km/h).
This performance exceeds the top speeds recorded by the worldʼs fastest racing sailboats: 55.6 knots for the AC75s of the Americaʼs Cup, and 55.06 knots for the F50s on the SailGP circuit.
This progress is no accident—
the team has since logged multiple runs between 55 and 58 knots,
sometimes in less-than-ideal wind conditions.
“This is a major milestone for the entire team.
Very few sailboats in history have broken the 100 km/h barrier, and we’re now tangibly closing in on our ultimate goal. What’s especially encouraging is being able to repeat those speeds multiple times throughout the week. It confirms not only the boat’s reliability, but also its capacity to go even faster. From here, the work continues: analyzing the data on land, and refining our handling on the water as soon as the wind allows.”
Mayeul van den Broek
SP80 boat pilot
The short-term objective for SP80 is clear: hold these speeds over 500 meters, as only
the average speed over this distance is eligible for official world record certification.
“We know the boat’s potential—now it’s up to us to become more precise
in our handling.
We’re discovering how the boat behaves beyond 100 km/h and learning to control it. This week, we came close several times to averaging 50 knots over 500 meters. It’s naturally a bit frustrating to end the week at 48.6, but we know it’s only a matter of time. Every run helps us improve, and our coordination with Mayeul is sharpening with each outing.”
Benoit Gaudiot
Kite pilot onboard SP80
48.645 KNOTS OVER 500 METERS:
WE’RE CLOSING IN ON OUR FIRST RECORD ATTEMPTS
With an average of 48.645 knots (90 km/h) over 500 meters,
we are now within reach of official records
that could be certified by the
WSSRC
(World Sailing Speed Record Council).
The first targets are category records, including:
50.07 knots average – Macquarie Innovation (2009)
, world record in Category C (sail area between 21 and 27 m²)
51.36 knots average – l’Hydroptère (2009)
, world record in Category D (sail area over 27 m²)
Both of these milestones could fall in the coming weeks, allowing
us to officially add our name to the list of world sailing speed record holders.
Our ultimate ambition remains unchanged:
to break the absolute world speed sailing record set by Paul Larsen aboard Vestas Sailrocket II
, with an average of 65.45 knots over 500 meters.
That means SP80 still needs to gain
16 knots
— a formidable challenge, but one we’re ready to take on with everything we’ve got!

data.title: Muon g-2 announces most precise measurement of the magnetic anomaly of the muon
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 科学家们发布了Muon g-2实验的第三次也是最终的μ子磁反常测量结果，该结果与此前2021年和2023年的结果一致，但精度大幅提升，达到127 parts-per-billion，超越了最初140 parts-per-billion的设计目标。这一结果为粒子物理标准模型提供了严格的检验，并成为未来多年内全球最精确的μ子磁反常测量值。尽管理论预测面临挑战，但该实验为探索新物理现象提供了重要基准。实验的圆满成功不仅实现了预期目标，还超出了预期，成为μ子研究中的重要里程碑。

44197201.article_content:
The third and final result, based on the last three years of data, is in perfect agreement with the experiment’s previous results, further solidifying the experimental world average. This long-awaited value will be the world’s most precise measurement of the muon magnetic anomaly for many years to come.
Media contact
Tracy Marc, Fermilab
media@fnal.gov
, 224-290-7803
Scientists working on the
Muon g-2 experiment
, hosted by the U.S. Department of Energy’s Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory, have released their third and final measurement of the muon magnetic anomaly. This value is related to g-2, the experiment’s namesake measurement. The final result agrees with their published results from 2021 and 2023 but with a much better precision of 127 parts-per-billion, surpassing the original experimental design goal of 140 parts-per-billion.
“The anomalous magnetic moment, or g–2
,
of the muon is important because it provides a sensitive test of the Standard Model of particle physics. This is an exciting result and it is great to see an experiment come to a definitive end with a precision measurement,” said Regina Rameika, the U.S. Department of Energy’s Associate Director for the Office of High Energy Physics.
“This is a very exciting moment because we not only achieved our goals but exceeded them …”
Peter Winter
Muon g-2 collaboration co-spokesperson
This long-awaited result is a tremendous achievement of precision and will remain the world’s most precise measurement of the muon magnetic anomaly for many years to come. Despite recent challenges with the theoretical predictions that reduce evidence of new physics from muon g-2, this result provides a stringent benchmark for proposed extensions of the Standard Model of particle physics.
“This is a very exciting moment because we not only achieved our goals but exceeded them, which is not very easy for these precision measurements,” said Peter Winter, a physicist at Argonne National Laboratory and co-spokesperson for the Muon g-2 collaboration. “With the support of the funding agencies and the host lab, Fermilab, it has been very successful overall, as we reached or surpassed pretty much all the items that we were aiming for.”
“For over a century, g-2 has been teaching us a lot about the nature of nature,” said Lawrence Gibbons, professor at Cornell University and analysis co-coordinator for this result. “It’s exciting to add a precise measurement that I think will stand for a long time.”
The third and final result from the Muon g-2 collaboration, based on the last three years of data, is in perfect agreement with the previous results, further solidifying the experimental world average. Credit: Muon g-2 collaboration
The Muon g-2 (pronounced “gee minus two”) experiment looks at the wobble of a fundamental particle called the
muon
. Muons are similar to electrons but about 200 times more massive; like electrons, muons have a quantum mechanical property called spin that can be interpreted as a tiny internal magnet. In the presence of an external magnetic field, the internal magnet will wobble — or precess — like the axis of a spinning top.
The precession speed in a magnetic field depends on properties of the muon described by a number called the g-factor. Theoretical physicists calculate the g-factor based on the current knowledge of how the universe works at a fundamental level, which is contained in the
Standard Model
of particle physics.
Nearly 100 years ago, the value of g was predicted to be 2. But experimental measurements soon showed g to be slightly different from 2 by a quantity known as the magnetic anomaly of the muon, a
μ
, calculated with (g-2)/2. The Muon g-2 experiment gets its name from this relation.
The muon magnetic anomaly encodes the effects of all Standard Model particles, and theoretical physicists can calculate these contributions to an incredible precision. But previous measurements taken
at Brookhaven National Laboratory
in the late 1990s and early 2000s showed a possible discrepancy with the theoretical calculation at that time.
When experiment doesn’t align with theory, it could indicate new physics. Specifically, physicists wondered if this discrepancy could be caused by as-yet undiscovered particles pulling at the muon’s precession.
So physicists decided to upgrade the Muon g-2 experiment to make a more precise measurement. In 2013, Brookhaven’s magnetic storage ring was
transported
from Long Island, New York, to Fermilab in Batavia, Illinois. After years of significant upgrades and improvements, the Fermilab Muon g-2 experiment started up on
May 31, 2017
.
The June 3, 2025 results from Fermilab represents analysis of the experiment’s best-quality data as a result of tweaks and enhancements to the experiment in 2023 that improved the quality of the muon beam and reduced uncertainties. Credit: Ryan Postel, Fermilab

data.title: Self-hosting your own media considered harmful according to YouTube
data.author: DavideNL
data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了自己在YouTube上因展示如何使用LibreELEC和Jellyfin自建媒体库而收到社区指导违规的经历。尽管视频内容仅涉及自建合法媒体库，并未涉及任何盗版或绕过付费订阅的工具，YouTube仍以“危险或有害内容”为由删除了视频。这已不是作者第一次遇到此类问题，之前关于Jellyfin的视频也曾被下架，但上诉后恢复。此次上诉却被驳回，令作者感到困惑和沮丧。作者将视频重新上传至Internet Archive和Floatplane，并讨论了在其他平台如Peertube上发布内容的挑战，尤其是这些平台的受众规模较小，难以实现内容创作的可持续性。作者感谢Patreon、GitHub和Floatplane支持者，并希望未来能找到直接资助以持续支持其工作。同时，对YouTube的AI摘要功能可能用于其AI模型表示担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：YouTube内容审核与删除、平台政策对创作者的影响、平台替代方案

不同观点：
• **关于内容审核和删除**：
  - [w14] 认为YouTube对与新冠相关内容的删除只是个开始，后续可能会有更多话题被纳入审查范围。特别提到Ofcom在英国实施的《在线安全法》可能会导致更多内容的审查，且平台会因为潜在的处罚而采取过于谨慎的内容删除策略。
  - [KurSix] 指出YouTube的审核机制不够精准，经常遗漏上下文，比如误删与开源和自托管相关的内容，而一些真正的盗版内容却长期存在。
  
• **关于平台政策对创作者的影响**：
  - [hardwaresofton] 提到YouTube的AdSense收入和广泛影响力像“金手铐”一样束缚着创作者。虽然对平台的依赖性在减弱，但要完全离开YouTube依然困难。同时，对未来互联网内容创作的新模式提出疑问，比如AI可能带来的改变。
  - [sp0ck] 和 [neepi] 都提到YouTube对特定内容（如枪支相关视频）的审核过于严格且模糊，导致合法内容的误删。创作者对此感到不满，并考虑其他方式观看或分发内容。

• **关于平台替代方案**：
  - [gloosx] 和 [neepi] 提到使用工具如yt-dlp下载YouTube视频，以此避免广告和内容限制。
  - [Helmut10001] 提出疑问，为什么还需要YouTube等视频托管平台，建议直接使用静态网页服务器托管视频。
  - [DavideNL] 和 [davedx] 提到Mastodon等去中心化平台和社区对内容创作和分享的影响，提到创作者可能转向其他平台。

补充讨论：
• **关于版权和盗版问题**：
  - [BLKNSLVR] 和 [qilo] 提到YouTube在版权检测方面的双重标准，比如误删合法内容，而盗版内容却长期存在。同时，对YouTube使用创作者内容训练AI模型的做法表示不满。
  - [boomboomsubban] 认为将某些内容标记为“危险或有害内容”是不合理的，特别是当这些内容并不鼓励盗版时。

争议焦点：YouTube内容审核的准确性和透明度、平台对创作者的限制与创作者自由之间的平衡、未来内容创作和分发的新模式。

44197932.article_content:
Self-hosting your own media considered harmful
I just received my
second community guidelines violation
for my video demonstrating the use of LibreELEC on a Raspberry Pi 5, for 4K video playback.
I purposefully avoid demonstrating any of the tools (with a suffix that rhymes with "car") that are popularly used to circumvent purchasing movie, TV, and other media content, or any tools that automatically slurp up YouTube content.
In fact, in my own house, for multiple decades, I've purchased physical media (CDs, DVDs, and more recently, Blu-Rays), and only have legally-acquired content on my NAS. Streaming services used to be a panacea but are now fragmented and mostly full of garbage—and lots of ads. We just wanted to be able to watch TV shows and movies without hassle (and I'm happy to pay for physical media that I want to watch).
But this morning, as I was finishing up work on a video about a new mini Pi cluster, I got a cheerful email from YouTube saying my video on LibreELEC on the Pi 5 was removed because it promoted:
Dangerous or Harmful Content
Content that describes how to get unauthorized or free access to audio or audiovisual content, software, subscription services, or games that usually require payment isn't allowed on YouTube.
I never described any of that stuff, only how to self-host your own media library.
This wasn't my first rodeo—in October last year, I got a
strike for showing people how to install Jellyfin
!
In
that
case, I was happy to see my appeal granted within an hour of the strike being placed on the channel. (Nevermind the fact the video had been live for
over two years
at that point, with nary a problem!)
So I thought, this case will be similar:
The video's been up for over a year, without issue
The video's had over half a million views
The video doesn't promote or highlight any tools used to circumvent copyright, get around paid subscriptions, or reproduce any content illegally
Slam-dunk, right? Well, not according to whomever reviewed my appeal. Apparently self-hosted open source media library management is harmful.
Who knew open source software could be so
subversive
?
The video
So along that theme, I've re-uploaded the video to Internet Archive, free for anyone to download and view at their leisure.
Yes, even those rebels running LibreELEC on their Raspberry Pis!
Here it is:
LibreELEC on the Raspberry Pi 5 - Internet Archive
.
I've also uploaded it
on Floatplane
, for subscribers.
Alternatives
I've been slowly uploading my back catalog to
my channel on Floatplane
, though not all my content is there yet.
Some in the fediverse ask why I'm not on Peertube. Here's the problem (and it's not insurmountable):
right now
, there's no easy path towards sustainable content production when the audience for the content is 100x smaller, and the number of patrons/sponsors remains proportionally the same.
I was never able to sustain my open source work based on patronage, and content production is the same—just more expensive to maintain to any standard (each video takes between 10-300 hours to produce, and I have a family to feed, and
US health insurance companies to fund
).
YouTube was, and still is, a creative anomaly. I'm hugely thankful to my
Patreon
,
GitHub
, and
Floatplane
supporters—and I hope to have direct funding fully able to support my work someday. But until that time, YouTube's AdSense revenue and vast reach is a kind of 'golden handcuff.'
The handcuff has been a bit tarnished of late, however, with Google recently adding AI summaries to videos—which
seems
to indicate maybe
Gemini is slurping up my content and using it in their AI models
?
Maybe the handcuffs are fools-gold, and I just don't see it yet.
Further reading
YouTube scares me; I need RAID 1 for my video content
Streaming services lost the plot
Can the Raspberry Pi 5 handle 4K?

data.author: nativeit
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了一个关于iSpindel设备的视频内容。视频中展示了Jeffrey 2.69型号的新功能，演示了一种平坦焊接技术，并使用一种新方法将iSpindel平衡至25度。视频重点讲解了如何通过焊盘重量来实现平衡，为使用者提供了实用的操作指导。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：家庭酿酒（蒸馏）过程中使用开源软件（OSS）及相关技术的必要性和合理性，以及家庭酿酒的合法性与个人喜好。

不同观点：
• [反对使用OSS] @dylan604 认为蒸馏过程本质上非常简单，不需要任何开源软件（OSS）的参与。他将这种情况比作家用电器（如洗衣机、烘干机、洗碗机）不需要联网功能，强调蒸馏过程的基本操作（发酵、煮沸、收集）不需要复杂技术支持。

• [支持技术介入] @01100011 则持不同意见，指出有些人可能不愿意在蒸馏开始时手动操作等待温度上升，暗示技术可以帮助简化这些步骤。他还表达了个人对蒸馏过程的享受，认为这是一种有趣的爱好，尤其对那些喜欢酿造的人来说值得尝试。

• [法律风险] @ghushn3 提出警告，强调在许多国家和美国的一些地区，家庭酿酒是严格非法的。他提醒人们在开始之前要谨慎考虑法律问题，以免触犯法律。

补充讨论：
- @01100011 提到蒸馏过程中热乙醇会产生类似钻石般闪耀的效果，这可能增加了蒸馏作为爱好的吸引力。
- 争议焦点在于是否需要技术（OSS）辅助简化蒸馏过程。@dylan604 认为这是不必要的复杂化，而@01100011 则认为技术可以提升体验。
- 另一个值得注意的点是家庭酿酒的合法性问题，@ghushn3 强调了在某些地区从事这一活动的法律风险。

data.title: Prompt engineering playbook for programmers
data.author: vinhnx
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于"提示工程"（prompt engineering）的定义、价值和必要性的讨论

不同观点：
• 支持提示工程：
  - **DebtDeflation**: 认为提示工程包括情境学习（In Context Learning）、思维链（Chain of Thought）和结构化输出等技术，强调明确语言描述的重要性，同时提及角色提示（Role Prompting）和RAG（检索增强生成）等方法。
  - **orochimaaru**: 通过科学编程课程中学到的验证方法来设计提示，认为正式指定输入、前提条件和后置条件可以生成有效的代码。
  
• 反对提示工程：
  - **bsoles**: 认为"提示工程"并非真正的工程，不过是写出合理句子的能力，质疑其专业性和必要性。
  - **leshow**: 认为使用"工程"一词描述写提示是不严肃的。
  - **jwr**: 认为提示工程不过是尝试和错误的过程，没有科学规律或法则，不属于科学或工程范畴。
  
• 对提示工程的实用性持怀疑态度：
  - **haolez**: 认为过于复杂和冗长的提示可能降低模型性能，主张使用简单和最小化的提示，通过少量迭代进行微调。
  - **heisenburgzero**: 认为如果问题本身无法由大型语言模型（LLM）解决，任何提示工程也无济于事，只有通过分解任务或示例部分解决。
  
• 对提示工程的替代方案：
  - **jorge_cab**: 认为开发者不应负责写"好提示"，建议通过中间层优化传递给LLM的信息，类似于Agentic IDEs正在做的。
  
• 对提示工程的心理抵触：
  - **BuyMyBitcoins**: 对用自然英语给出提示有心理障碍，认为应该像写SQL查询或提供可执行参数那样精确，但承认自然语言处理使工具更易访问。
  
• 彻底反对依赖提示工程：
  - **akkad33**: 宁愿自己写代码，也不愿依赖提示工程。
  
• 对软件工程行业现状的批评：
  - **nexoft**: 认为"提示工程"是痛苦的，并批评软件工程行业因过度追求薪酬而导致工程师质量下降，提示工程成为拐杖。

补充讨论：
• 提示工程的工具和实践：
  - **ColinEberhardt**: 认为目前过多的提示指南不必要，熟悉工具和其工作方式后，合适的提示自然会显现。
  
• 对提示工程的幽默和讽刺：
  - **air7**: 引用Sergey Brin的话，以幽默方式提到威胁模型以获得更好结果，反映出对提示工程的非传统看法。

争议焦点：
• 提示工程是否属于真正的工程范畴及其专业性。
• 提示工程的复杂性是否有助于提升模型性能或适得其反。
• 开发者是否应负责写提示或通过工具和中间层优化提示。

data.title: FFmpeg merges WebRTC support
data.author: Sean-Der
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了网站管理员为保护服务器免受AI公司大量抓取数据导致的宕机问题，而设置了一个名为Anubis的系统。Anubis采用了一种类似于Hashcash的“工作量证明”机制，旨在增加大规模数据抓取的成本。虽然对普通用户影响不大，但在面对大规模抓取时能有效增加其成本。Anubis是一个临时解决方案，旨在为更复杂的真实用户识别技术争取时间。需要注意的是，Anubis需要使用现代JavaScript功能，因此需要禁用如JShelter等插件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WebRTC广播及其相关技术（如WHIP协议）在不同场景中的应用和潜在问题。

不同观点：
• **支持与兴奋态度**：
   - [Sean-Der] 对WebRTC广播和WHIP协议的广泛支持感到兴奋，认为这是视频广播领域的一个重要里程碑，特别是在跨平台（移动、网页、嵌入式设备等）上的应用。
   - [msgodel] 认为这将使自托管流媒体或流媒体CDN变得更加容易，特别是如果熟悉FFmpeg的话，它是非常强大的媒体软件。
   - [FrostKiwi] 期待使用FFmpeg和WebRTC流来简化当前的远程控制项目，避免复杂的ExpressJS操作。

• **技术实现与未来发展**：
   - [jauntywundrkind] 提到虽然WHIP使用了WebRTC的SCTP协议，但更希望未来能转向基于QUIC或WebTransport的P2P协议，如Media-over-QUIC (MoQ)，因为QUIC能更好地处理UDP上的多路复用和复杂性。
   - [qwertox] 询问WHIP是否意味着网站可以直接连接到FFmpeg实例并接收音视频流，有人提供了FFmpeg WHIP相关信息的链接。

• **潜在问题与安全性担忧**：
   - [autoexec] 担心WebRTC的安全性问题，指出WebRTC的漏洞曾导致许多安全事件，通常会在安装浏览器后禁用它。
   - [throwpoaster] 关心FFmpeg的安全审计机制，认为其目前看起来较为被动。

• **具体应用场景与技术问题**：
   - [esbeeb] 提到Gajim（XMPP客户端）一直等待此功能以恢复其音视频通话功能，FFmpeg的WHIP支持将大大简化这一过程。
   - [pkz] 询问FFmpeg是否能录制Jitsi视频会议的音频流。
   - [leland-takamine] 寻求帮助，希望了解如何从源代码构建包含WHIP支持的FFmpeg。
   - [SeriousM] 期待看到此功能在Jellyfin中的实现。

• **其他讨论与用户体验问题**：
   - [tyre] 和 [dyl000] 提到他们在iOS Safari上遇到机器人检测问题，其中一位用户通过Anubis解决了问题，另一位则未能成功。
   - [chompychop] 作为初学者，询问WebRTC是否可以替代base64编码图像传输用于后端图像处理，并询问这种方法是否推荐。

补充讨论：
- WHIP协议的引入对多平台视频广播的影响。
- 关于FFmpeg和WebRTC技术在具体项目中的应用潜力与技术挑战。
- 安全性与隐私问题在WebRTC和FFmpeg使用中的重要性。
- 用户在不同平台和应用场景中遇到的实际问题，如iOS兼容性和编译问题。

44182186.article_content:
Making sure you're not a bot!
Loading...
Why am I seeing this?
You are seeing this because the administrator of this website has set up
Anubis
to protect the server against the scourge of
AI companies aggressively scraping websites
. This can and does cause downtime for the websites, which makes their resources inaccessible for everyone.
Anubis is a compromise. Anubis uses a
Proof-of-Work
scheme in the vein of
Hashcash
, a proposed proof-of-work scheme for reducing email spam. The idea is that at individual scales the additional load is ignorable, but at mass scraper levels it adds up and makes scraping much more expensive.
Ultimately, this is a hack whose real purpose is to give a "good enough" placeholder solution so that more time can be spent on fingerprinting and identifying headless browsers (EG: via how they do font rendering) so that the challenge proof of work page doesn't need to be presented to users that are much more likely to be legitimate.
Please note that Anubis requires the use of modern JavaScript features that plugins like
JShelter
will disable. Please disable JShelter or other such plugins for this domain.

   - [Sean-Der] 对WebRTC广播和WHIP协议的广泛支持感到兴奋，认为这是视频广播领域的一个重要里程碑，特别是在跨平台（移动、网页、嵌入式设备等）上的应用。
   - [msgodel] 认为这将使自托管流媒体或流媒体CDN变得更加容易，特别是如果熟悉FFmpeg的话，它是非常强大的媒体软件。
   - [FrostKiwi] 期待使用FFmpeg和WebRTC流来简化当前的远程控制项目，避免复杂的ExpressJS操作。

• **技术实现与未来发展**：
   - [jauntywundrkind] 提到虽然WHIP使用了WebRTC的SCTP协议，但更希望未来能转向基于QUIC或WebTransport的P2P协议，如Media-over-QUIC (MoQ)，因为QUIC能更好地处理UDP上的多路复用和复杂性。
   - [qwertox] 询问WHIP是否意味着网站可以直接连接到FFmpeg实例并接收音视频流，有人提供了FFmpeg WHIP相关信息的链接。

• **潜在问题与安全性担忧**：
   - [autoexec] 担心WebRTC的安全性问题，指出WebRTC的漏洞曾导致许多安全事件，通常会在安装浏览器后禁用它。
   - [throwpoaster] 关心FFmpeg的安全审计机制，认为其目前看起来较为被动。

• **具体应用场景与技术问题**：
   - [esbeeb] 提到Gajim（XMPP客户端）一直等待此功能以恢复其音视频通话功能，FFmpeg的WHIP支持将大大简化这一过程。
   - [pkz] 询问FFmpeg是否能录制Jitsi视频会议的音频流。
   - [leland-takamine] 寻求帮助，希望了解如何从源代码构建包含WHIP支持的FFmpeg。
   - [SeriousM] 期待看到此功能在Jellyfin中的实现。

• **其他讨论与用户体验问题**：
   - [tyre] 和 [dyl000] 提到他们在iOS Safari上遇到机器人检测问题，其中一位用户通过Anubis解决了问题，另一位则未能成功。
   - [chompychop] 作为初学者，询问WebRTC是否可以替代base64编码图像传输用于后端图像处理，并询问这种方法是否推荐。

补充讨论：
- WHIP协议的引入对多平台视频广播的影响。
- 关于FFmpeg和WebRTC技术在具体项目中的应用潜力与技术挑战。
- 安全性与隐私问题在WebRTC和FFmpeg使用中的重要性。
- 用户在不同平台和应用场景中遇到的实际问题，如iOS兼容性和编译问题。

data.title: Cursor 1.0
data.author: ecz
data.article_summary: Cursor 1.0发布，主要更新包括：引入BugBot进行自动代码审查，发现问题后可一键修复；Background Agent功能对所有用户开放，支持通过云图标或快捷键访问，隐私模式下也将 soon 支持；Background Agent现可在Jupyter Notebooks中使用，支持Sonnet模型；推出Memories功能，可记忆对话事实并在未来引用，目前为测试功能；MCP服务器支持一键安装和OAuth认证；聊天响应增强，支持Mermaid图表和Markdown表格；设置和仪表盘页面更新，提供使用统计和团队管理功能等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cursor（一个基于VSCode的AI辅助开发工具）的商业模式、技术问题、用户体验以及与VSCode和其它AI工具的竞争关系。

不同观点：
• [ai_assisted_dev] 认为 Cursor 的收费标准不切实际，尽管他个人通过使用 Cursor 提高了工作效率，但 Cursor 的高成本（尤其是API请求费用）让人担忧其盈利模式。他还提到希望增加异步请求等功能以提升效率。
• [BudaDude] 喜欢 Cursor，但担心其扩展更新速度慢以及多个MCP服务器实例导致内存占用过大的问题。
• [ashleynewman] 对那些与Cursor发布无关的抱怨表示不满，并特别关注BugBot的发布，希望它不仅仅是查看代码差异，还能利用完整的上下文进行代码审查。
• [vladstudio] 推荐了ampcode.com，并表示其使用Claude 4且无需设置，使用体验良好。
• [blixt] 提到Cursor与VSCode的兼容性问题，尤其是与微软开发的插件和容器化工具的兼容性问题，并指出Cursor逐渐偏离VSCode的设计。
• [jameslk] 提出Cursor的愿望清单，希望在代码审查中能更清楚地标识模型修改代码的原因，以减少调试困难。
• [jimrandomh] 批评Cursor作为闭源的VSCode分支，在插件支持上存在问题，且缺乏文档支持，认为这是对开源项目的不尊重。
• [swyx] 认为Cursor的1.0发布过于低调，缺乏市场推广和愿景描述，导致用户难以形成明确预期。
• [CafeRacer] 已经放弃使用Cursor，主要因为其不稳定的表现和IDE中的干扰性自动完成功能，同时提到VSCode市场不再适用于Cursor。
• [jadbox] 认为任何闭源的VSCode替代品都无法与VSCode加上多个开源扩展（如Copilot、CLINE、FOAM）竞争。
• [curiousElf] 希望Cursor能更好地支持多根目录仓库，并提到模型经常选错目录，需要手动引导。
• [mythz] 认为Cursor尝试创建自己的IDE是一个战略错误，并表示只会考虑集成到现有IDE（如VSCode和Rider）中的AI工具。
• [dkersten] 停止使用Cursor，转而使用Zed的代理模式，因为Cursor存在内存泄漏问题，且Zed更轻量。
• [sidgarimella] 提到同时运行多个IDE和终端会话，使用Claude Code，并通过Neuralink直接连接到MCP服务器，认为不同的工具在不同场景下各有用途。
• [serverlessmania] 认为Cursor作为VSCode的分支没有足够的理由让开发者放弃现有的工具（如Vim、JetBrains、VSCode），并预测随着终端代理（如Claude Code和Codex）的兴起，Cursor将变得过时。

补充讨论：
• 收费争议：[ai_assisted_dev] 和 [jimrandomh] 对Cursor的收费模式和闭源性质提出质疑，认为当前收费不合理且对开源社区不尊重。
• 功能需求：[ai_assisted_dev]、[jameslk] 和 [curiousElf] 提出了对Cursor功能改进的愿望，如异步请求、代码修改原因标识和多根目录支持。
• 竞争与替代：[mythz]、[CafeRacer]、[jadbox] 和 [serverlessmania] 讨论了Cursor与VSCode及其它AI工具（如Copilot、Claude Code）的竞争关系，认为Cursor面临巨大挑战。
• 技术问题：[BudaDude]、[blixt] 和 [dkersten] 提到了Cursor在扩展兼容性、内存管理和性能方面的技术问题。

Jun 4, 2025
1.0
BugBot, Background Agent access to everyone, and one-click MCP install
Cursor 1.0 is here!
This release brings BugBot for code review, a first look at memories, one-click MCP setup, Jupyter support, and general availability of Background Agent.
Automatic code review with BugBot
BugBot automatically reviews your PRs and catches potential bugs and issues.
When an issue is found, BugBot leaves a comment on your PRs in GitHub. You can click "
Fix in Cursor
" to move back to the editor with a pre-filled prompt to fix the issue.
To set it up, follow instructions in our
BugBot docs
.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Background Agent for everyone
Since we released Background Agent, our remote coding agent, in early access a few weeks ago, early signals have been positive.
We're now excited to expand Background Agent to all users! You can start using it right away by clicking the cloud icon in chat or hitting
Cmd/Ctrl+E
if you have privacy mode disabled. For users with privacy mode enabled, we'll soon have a way to enable it for you too!
Agent in Jupyter Notebooks
Cursor can now implement changes in Jupyter Notebooks!
Agent will now create and edit multiple cells directly inside of Jupyter, a significant improvement for research and data science tasks. Only supported with Sonnet models to start.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Memories
With Memories, Cursor can remember facts from conversations and reference them in the future. Memories are stored per project on an individual level, and can be managed from Settings.
We're rolling out Memories as a beta feature. To get started, enable from Settings → Rules.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
MCP one-click install and OAuth support
You can now set up MCP servers in Cursor with one click, and together with OAuth support, you can easily authenticate servers that support it.
We've curated a short list of official MCP servers you can add to Cursor at
docs.cursor.com/tools
.
If you're an MCP developer, you can easily make your server available to developers by adding a
Add to Cursor
button in your documentation and READMEs. Generate one at
docs.cursor.com/deeplinks
.

Richer Chat responses
Cursor can now render visualizations inside of a conversation. In particular, Mermaid diagrams and Markdown tables can now be generated and viewed in the same place!

New Settings and Dashboard
The setting and dashboard page have gotten some polish with this release.
With the new Dashboard, you can view your individual or team's usage analytics, update your display name, and view detailed statistics broken down by tool or model.

data.title: Amelia Earhart's Reckless Final Flights
data.author: Thevet
data.article_summary: 1937年，著名女飞行员阿梅莉亚·埃尔哈特（Amelia Earhart）试图驾驶洛克希德Electra 10-E飞机进行环球飞行，但在夏威夷的路克机场起飞时发生事故。飞机在跑道上失控旋转，幸好没有爆炸，埃尔哈特和两名导航员安全脱险。埃尔哈特此前因横跨大西洋的飞行而闻名，但她实际操作经验不足，且忙于宣传活动，缺乏充分准备。她的飞行依赖于导航员的帮助，且飞机技术先进但操控复杂。此次环球飞行计划长达29,000英里，途经豪兰岛等偏远地点，面临巨大风险。尽管如此，成功将带来巨大的声誉和商业机会。媒体对她的冒险高度关注，但她最终在尝试中失踪。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Amelia Earhart的飞行悲剧及其历史评价的多角度讨论

不同观点：
• **技术失误论**：cylinder714引用1993年美国海军学会的文章，认为Earhart的悲剧是由于无线电设备操作不当，特别是有人在她飞行前拆除了一个用于长距离通讯的可伸缩天线，这一技术失误是导致她失踪的重要原因。

• **历史背景论**：a-r-t提到Veritasium的一个视频深入探讨了她最后一次飞行的技术细节和问题，暗示飞行失败不仅仅是个人失误，还涉及当时的技术局限和风险。

• **个人评价论**：WalterBright分享其父亲作为B-17导航员和职业飞行员的看法，认为Earhart是个鲁莽的飞行员，并表示对她缺乏敬意，但同时对另一位女性飞行员Jacqueline Cochran表示钦佩，以证明其并非性别歧视。

• **历史地位论**：cameldrv指出Earhart因媒体宣传而广为人知，但实际上第一个完成环球飞行的女性并非她，而是被大众忽视，反映出公众记忆的选择性。

• **历史教训论**：beedeebeedee认为Earhart的飞行失败是当时航空发展阶段中常见的鲁莽飞行现象之一，并提到20世纪20年代阿拉斯加丛林飞行员的冒险故事，强调集体学习飞行技术的重要性。

• **英雄形象论**：0xbadcafebee表示喜欢这类历史故事，认为成为历史人物往往需要一些“疯狂”的举动，同时指出没有必要粉饰或掩盖英雄的缺陷，因为他们的传奇往往会继续流传。

• **文字编辑批评**：johnyzee对文章中使用"coördinated"这种带分音符号的拼写方式表示不满，认为这种用法显得过于正式和过时。

• **语义质疑**：bauble对文章中“人类导航员”的表述提出质疑，认为用“男性导航员”可能更为准确，因为Earhart本身也是人类一员，这种表述显得逻辑不通。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及到对历史事件的多角度审视，包括技术失误、个人性格、历史地位以及公众记忆的选择性等问题。
• 部分评论还涉及对媒体、语言使用以及历史人物形象的批判性思考。
• 争议焦点在于Earhart作为飞行员的专业能力和其历史地位是否被过度宣传，以及技术失误在其失踪事件中的实际影响。

Sparks flew, a wing bent, and the landing gear snapped off as the silver Lockheed Electra 10-E plane smashed into the runway at Luke Field, outside Honolulu. The pilot’s only stroke of luck was that the aircraft, which contained nearly a thousand gallons of fuel, didn’t explode.
The thirty-nine-year-old Amelia Earhart and her crew of two navigators, Fred Noonan and Harry Manning, crawled out of the wreckage, unsettled but otherwise unhurt. They had meant to depart on the second leg of a gruelling voyage: a round-the-world flight that had begun in Oakland, California, and would continue westward, with two dozen or so stops, before ending up back in Oakland. People close to Earhart knew that she wasn’t fully ready for a challenge of this magnitude, and so a work-around had been devised. An extra crew member with extensive flight experience, Paul Mantz, had joined the flight to Hawaii. On the runway in Oakland, he switched places with Earhart and assumed the throttles during takeoff. She then piloted most of the way to Oahu, but Mantz often took over.
As they approached Luke Field, Mantz sensed that Earhart had “pilot fatigue.” He asked her, “Do you want to land it?”
“No, you land it,” Earhart said.
He did so, then said farewell. Earhart had been able to observe Mantz’s handling of the plane over the Pacific, and from now on she would be the only pilot onboard. Flying the Electra solo wouldn’t be easy. Although the plane had state-of-the-art technology for its time, piloting it demanded constant coördination among the throttle, the rudder, and the control column—especially during takeoff and landing. While taking off on the second leg, Earhart ignored advice that Mantz had given her not to “jockey the throttles”—change the speed to maintain direction and balance—and the plane veered into a violent spin across the runway. The press had assembled to watch Earhart soar, and instead witnessed an embarrassment.
The stakes were huge. Men had been flying around the world since 1924, when a team of eight military officers completed a twenty-seven-thousand-mile journey in a hundred and seventy-five days (with seventy-four stops). Only one pilot had done a solo circumnavigation: a Texan named Wiley Post. In 1933, Post completed a fifteen-thousand-mile journey, traversing Germany, the Soviet Union, Alaska, and Canada. Four years later, a round-the-world flight remained daunting. Earhart planned to have human navigators on board with her, but she’d be the first female pilot to accomplish the feat.
Earhart had become instantly famous in 1928, as the first woman to cross the Atlantic in a plane. But, though she’d been photographed wearing a flight suit and a leather helmet, she was merely a passenger; the plane had actually been piloted by two men, Wilmer Stultz and Louis Gordon. She had since been working on establishing her command of the cockpit. There were plenty of accomplished female pilots who could’ve taken command of a transatlantic flight themselves, and some of these women considered Earhart’s notoriety unearned. In 1932, after logging more flight miles—but not as many as other top female pilots—she flew solo across the Atlantic in a cramped red Vega, a single-engine plane barely insulated against storms and cold temperatures. She fought exhaustion, iced wings, and a broken altimeter. Her intention was to land in Paris, but she ended up in a cow field in Ireland. Earhart approached the experience with an easy, almost reckless, confidence. She’d always been this way; as a girl growing up in the Kansas City area, she jury-rigged a “roller coaster” with steep ramps, then barrelled down it and fell off, only to exult, “This is just like flying!”
A globe-circling flight would be Earhart’s lengthiest journey by far, twenty-nine thousand miles hugging the equator. This wasn’t mere hopping among landmasses, as with Post’s route. Her path had been ambitiously charted to include a refuelling stop on Howland Island, a speck between Hawaii and Australia. A pilot making such a journey needed to be in excellent shape, with sufficient strength and stamina to manage the controls in turbulence, particularly during long hours in a cockpit with no autopilot. The dangers were extraordinary: enormous stretches over open ocean, unpredictable weather, extended isolation, intense psychological pressure. Yet the rewards promised to be substantial, from marketing opportunities to media attention. NBC and CBS were fighting over the rights to exclusive broadcasts.
Noonan and Manning had agreed to accompany Earhart nearly the whole way. They were excited to be associated with her glamour, but they also considered the job a risk. Rather than spending time practicing in the powerful Electra, Earhart had been crisscrossing the country, giving lectures, making sponsorship appearances, and attending promotional events. For a while, she had a gig as the aviation editor at
Cosmopolitan
44185078.article_summary: 1937年，著名女飞行员阿梅莉亚·埃尔哈特（Amelia Earhart）试图驾驶洛克希德Electra 10-E飞机进行环球飞行，但在夏威夷的路克机场起飞时发生事故。飞机在跑道上失控旋转，幸好没有爆炸，埃尔哈特和两名导航员安全脱险。埃尔哈特此前因横跨大西洋的飞行而闻名，但她实际操作经验不足，且忙于宣传活动，缺乏充分准备。她的飞行依赖于导航员的帮助，且飞机技术先进但操控复杂。此次环球飞行计划长达29,000英里，途经豪兰岛等偏远地点，面临巨大风险。尽管如此，成功将带来巨大的声誉和商业机会。媒体对她的冒险高度关注，但她最终在尝试中失踪。
44185078.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• **技术失误论**：cylinder714引用1993年美国海军学会的文章，认为Earhart的悲剧是由于无线电设备操作不当，特别是有人在她飞行前拆除了一个用于长距离通讯的可伸缩天线，这一技术失误是导致她失踪的重要原因。

• **历史背景论**：a-r-t提到Veritasium的一个视频深入探讨了她最后一次飞行的技术细节和问题，暗示飞行失败不仅仅是个人失误，还涉及当时的技术局限和风险。

• **个人评价论**：WalterBright分享其父亲作为B-17导航员和职业飞行员的看法，认为Earhart是个鲁莽的飞行员，并表示对她缺乏敬意，但同时对另一位女性飞行员Jacqueline Cochran表示钦佩，以证明其并非性别歧视。

• **历史地位论**：cameldrv指出Earhart因媒体宣传而广为人知，但实际上第一个完成环球飞行的女性并非她，而是被大众忽视，反映出公众记忆的选择性。

• **历史教训论**：beedeebeedee认为Earhart的飞行失败是当时航空发展阶段中常见的鲁莽飞行现象之一，并提到20世纪20年代阿拉斯加丛林飞行员的冒险故事，强调集体学习飞行技术的重要性。

data.article_summary: AdamCAD是一个由AI驱动的CAD平台，可以在几秒钟内通过文字描述生成3D设计。用户可以通过文本提示创建和编辑3D模型，并进一步优化和导出设计。此外，AdamCAD还能将图像快速转换为3D模型，集成专业CAD软件，支持各种设计需求，如齿轮、支架、植物盆等模型。平台旨在通过自然语言帮助专业人士将创意变为现实，适用于工业设计和机械工程等领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI驱动3D模型工具的应用与功能改进

不同观点：
• arberavdullahu认为该工具在定制家具（如不同材质和设计选项）方面有很大潜力，并提到IKEA有类似应用。他提到工具在过度迭代时会改变物体形态，并建议结合高分辨率图片生成更逼真的渲染图。
• klaus silveira关注3D模型纹理的增强和重塑，分享了自己通过ComfyUI和Blender脚本实现的流程，并提出对网格简化和UV展开工具的需求，还询问了自动化绑定的可能性。
• lucasoshiro希望能够下载生成的.scad文件，并对工具在生成参数化模型（如瓶子）方面的失败表示失望，但总体上对工具表示肯定。
• chmod775对工具的表现超出预期，提到可以快速应用生成模型并进行修改，尽管模型不够完美，但比自己从头创建要快。
• adenta分享了自己在openSCAD和MCP方面的经验，并愿意提供帮助。
• Valk3_对Blender和openSCAD的功能进行比较，认为Blender在3D建模方面可能更强大，但实现类似工具可能更困难。
• WillAdams对工具的可用性表示失望，特别是对复杂模型的生成（如网格单元）失败，指出openSCAD在数学能力上的限制。
• ata_aman希望实现GPT支持的多物理仿真，设计CAD对象时希望通过语音转文本运行不同仿真。
• protocolture对工具的表现表示肯定，但指出工具在设计细节应用上的不足，并考虑在其他工具中完成设计。
• flippyhead对与孩子一起使用该工具进行3D打印表示兴奋，并好奇输出模型在prusa打印机上的效果。
• voidUpdate关注生成模型的拓扑结构问题，希望避免再次修复糟糕的拓扑。
• iancmceachern对工具与CAD软件的集成感兴趣，询问在Solidworks中使用的订阅级别。
• gavmor关注自支撑设计和参数化结构优化，询问工具如何与其他支持这些技术的流程结合。
• b0a04gl对工具在用户通过提示修改模型时的约束解决和几何验证机制感兴趣，询问是否维护共享参数模型或对比场景图，以及几何验证的处理方式。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是工具在生成复杂模型时的表现，部分用户（如WillAdams）对失败案例表示失望，而其他用户（如chmod775）则对工具的快速生成能力表示赞赏。
• 用户对工具与其他软件（如Blender、openSCAD、Solidworks）的集成和互补功能有较高兴趣，特别是自动化和优化方面的需求。
• 拓扑结构和模型质量是用户关注的重点，部分用户（如voidUpdate）希望避免修复糟糕的拓扑。
• 对工具的未来功能扩展（如多物理仿真、自支撑设计、自动化绑定）也有较多讨论，用户希望工具能在现有流程中更好地结合和应用。

data.title: Why I wrote the BEAM book
data.author: lawik
data.article_summary: 《BEAM书》的作者分享了撰写这本书的曲折经历和动机。在维护Klarna核心系统的十年中，他意识到即使是15毫秒的暂停也可能导致严重问题。他于2012年开始撰写此书，最初使用DocBook，后来转向AsciiDoc并编写自定义脚本，乐观预计六个月完成。然而，项目多次遭遇挫折，包括与O'Reilly和Pragmatic Bookshelf的出版合作相继取消。2017年，他在GitHub上重新启动项目，并获得社区贡献支持。书中涵盖了BEAM调度器、内存管理、垃圾回收、编译器和调试等方面，旨在为Erlang和Elixir系统开发和运维人员提供深入参考。作者强调，坚持比完美更重要，最终完成了这本深入解析BEAM的手册。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：BEAM 技术及其相关书籍、学习资源和应用情况

不同观点：
• elric 强调了对 BEAM 深入理解的驱动以及出版商与作者之间在选题上的分歧。他提到自己追求更深层次的技术内容，而非表面的解释，并且分享了与出版商在书籍主题上无法达成一致的经历。
• schonfinkel 高度评价了 BEAM 和 Erlang 技术，认为学习 BEAM 是他过去一年中最好的技术体验之一，并推荐了 Joe Armstrong 的书，同时对新出版的 BEAM 书籍表示赞赏。
• game_the0ry 认为 BEAM 是被低估的技术，并以 WhatsApp 为例，表示对 Elixir 和 Erlang 在高并发项目中未得到广泛应用的不解。
• bicx 表示 BEAM 和 Elixir 是他构建网络或管道密集系统的首选工具，虽然近期项目中不太适用，但仍乐于关注其发展，并对新出版的书籍表示欢迎。
• pyuser583 提到尽管 BEAM 的优点被广泛宣传，但其采用率仍然较低，对此表示疑惑。
• cgopalan 确认该书籍对有 Erlang/BEAM 经验的开发者更有用，并询问其对新手的适用性。

补充讨论：
• techpression 表示即使书籍可以在网上免费获取，仍然愿意购买以支持作者。
• asib 对 15ms 的后 mortem 事件表示不解，认为时间过短不足以引起如此重视。
• maerch 分享了 positive 网络评论对其产生的持久积极影响，强调了积极互动的重要性。
• graboid 提问是否存在其他类似 BEAM 的虚拟机，并探讨了开发新虚拟机的难度和工作量。
• spelunker 提到尽管 JVM 文档丰富，但 BEAM 对他而言仍然神秘，并对新资源表示欢迎。
• tra3 表示对未来能实际使用 Erlang 的期待。

争议焦点：
• BEAM 技术的采用率低，尽管其在高并发项目中表现出色，但未被广泛应用，这引起了多位评论者的讨论和不解。
• 出版选题上的分歧，尤其是技术作者与出版商在书籍主题选择上的矛盾。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• BEAM 技术的深度和复杂性使其学习资源显得稀缺和珍贵。
• 对技术社区中积极互动和支持的重视，如 techpression 对作者的支持和 maerch 对积极评论的感受。

44179257.article_content:
Hacker's Handbook
Why I Wrote the BEAM Book
Post-mortems, coffee, and a decade of stubborn curiosity
Posted:  2025-06-03
Categories:
development
,
Erlang
,
BEAM
,
theBeamBook
,
writing
Why I wrote the Beam Book
After ten years of keeping Klarnaâs core system upright I know this: a 15
millisecond pause in the BEAM can stall millions of peak-shopping payments, trigger a 3 a.m. Christmas-Eve post-mortem, and earn you a very awake call from the CEO. I wrote
The BEAM Book
so the next engineer fixes that pause before the coffee cools.
Origins
I opened the project on 12 October 2012 with a lone DocBook file with four lines of text and an oversized sense of optimism.
After two weeks, the commit log is mostly me adding structure, moving
headings, and updating metadata. Most of it is scaffolding. The actual
content is still just a few hopeful lines.
By November I had abandoned DocBook for AsciiDoc, written a custom build
script, and convinced myself the book could be wrapped up in six months.
Those early commits glow with energy: adds, rewrites, then more
rewrites to fix the rewrites.
Delusion is underrated.
In 2013 I managed to convince OâReilly to publish. Moving the repo to their
Atlas system sounded simple until Atlas began hiding my main file and
overwriting half-finished chapters.
The Git history reads like a diary of frustration:
âMoving files to top level to cope with Atlas,â âAtlas seems to be
overwriting book.asciidocâ. Word count shot past 120 000 while actual
progress crawled. On 10 March 2015 I was literally âSmashing chapters into sectionsâ just to keep the build green.
The quiet cancellation came two months later. No drama, just a polite call and a line through the contract. Relief mingled with embarrassment, I had spent two years rearranging files rather than finishing sentences.
Pragmatic Bookshelf took over that same year. I kept working in CVS for
their production system, but progress was slow. Eventually, they cancelled
too. On 20 January 2017, I imported everything into a new repo in one
massive commit: 6,622 files, over a million lines.
The rewrite stalled, and so did the project.
On 23 March 2017 I started fresh with Asciidoctor in a private GitHub repo, copy-pasting
only the parts that still made sense. Two weeks later, on April 7, minutes before
a lecture at Chalmers, I flipped the repository public. Within twenty-four
hours strangers fixed typos, added diagrams, and merged a Creative Commons
BY-4.0 license.
What Kept Me Going
I kept going because I wanted to understand the BEAM properly. Thereâs
value in following the real logic, not just the surface explanations.
Community feedback made a difference. As soon as the repo was public,
people began sending corrections, examples, and improvements.
Seeing the numbers of people starring the repo on GitHub kept me going.
One highlight:
Issue #113 - âPlease continue being awesome.â
That emoji-laced drive-by encouragement (August 2018) still pops into my
head whenever motivation dips.
The book started showing up as a reference in Erlang and BEAM conference
talks, sometimes several times in the same event. That was a clear signal
that others needed this as much as I did.
Even Twitter (in the good old days of Twitter) played a role. Whenever
someone mentioned the book or shared a
link, it was an extra nudge to keep at it.
Mostly, I just wanted a manual I could trust myself, a reference for the
parts of the VM that matter when things go wrong. Thatâs reason enough to
keep writing, even after the third rewrite.
Whatâs Inside the Book & Who It Helps
The book covers what I wish Iâd had when building and operating large
Erlang systems:
Schedulers and process management: How the BEAM schedules,
prioritizes, and balances processes under real load.
Processes and their memory: How process heaps,
stack, messages, and binaries are managed and
why these details matter in production.
Garbage collection and memory: What actually happens
with per-process and global garbage collectors, binary references,
and memory leaks.
Tagging schemes and terms: How the BEAM represents data-integers,
floats, tuples, binaries, references-down to the tagging bits.
The compiler and the VM: How code is turned into instructions,
what the compiler does (and doesnât do), and how the emulator executes it.
Tracing and debugging: Practical use of dbg, erlang:trace,
and other tools to follow messages, events, and identify bottlenecks.
Performance tuning: What matters when profiling real code,
understanding reductions, and tracking down real-world latency problems.
System architecture: How ERTS, the BEAM VM, and their subsystems
actually work together in a running node.
If you build or operate Erlang or Elixir systems, especially under any kind
of scale-this book is for you. It saves you from hunting through mailing
lists, scattered docs, and code comments just to answer, âWhy is the VM
behaving like this?â
Lessons Learned
Persistence beats perfection. Two can

data.title: UK Court Rules on Reverse Engineering of Mainframe Software
data.author: wslh
data.article_summary: 2025年5月13日，英国法院就大型机软件的反向工程问题作出裁决，IBM UK成功维护其软件许可协议的条款，对抗创建竞争产品的被告。法院强调严格遵守软件许可协议中的使用限制和潜在违约条款，尤其在涉及知识产权保护时，对版权例外采取限制性解释，以维护版权所有者的合法权益。此案中，Winsopia Ltd及其关联公司被发现利用IBM的许可软件协助开发竞争软件（SDM），违反了协议条款。法院最终判决禁止被告继续销售、推广或分发SDM软件，并要求销毁相关程序，同时IBM获赔诉讼费用。此判决提醒软件许可方应明确协议条款，而被许可方则需严格遵守约定，特别是在涉及反向工程和软件共享时。

In Short
The Situation
: IBM UK ("IBM") successfully enforced the terms of a mainframe license against the defendants who had created a competing software product.
The Result
: Focusing on the discussion of intellectual property rights, the court favored a strict adherence to the terms of the software license agreement when assessing use restrictions and potential breaches. Copyright exceptions conferred by Directive 2009/24/EC ("Software Directive") are limited and will be applied restrictively, ensuring that copyright owners are able to exploit their work and protect their legitimate interests.
Looking Ahead
: Software licensors should ensure that their agreements are sufficiently clear to protect their intellectual property interests. Likewise, software licensees should ensure that the terms of software license agreements are adhered to, especially where the software is decompiled and shared with related entities. Such use must be in relation to the acts permitted by the agreement.
Background
In 2013, the second defendant, Winsopia Ltd ("Winsopia"), entered into a customer agreement with the claimant, IBM (the "ICA"). Unbeknownst at the time to IBM, Winsopia is a wholly owned subsidiary of the third defendant, LzLabs UK, which was ultimately owned by the first defendant, LzLabs GmbH ("LzLabs"). The sixth defendant, Mr. John Moores, is the main beneficial owner of LzLabs, Winsopia, and LzLabs UK.
Notably, back in 2009, Mr. Moore's separate company, Neon Enterprise Software LLC ("Neon"), had unsuccessfully sued IBM Corporation in the United States. In that dispute, which concluded in 2011 and involved a counterclaim by IBM, an employee from Neon admitted to acts of reverse assembly and the destruction of evidence related to IBM Corporation's proprietary software. IBM succeeded in preventing Neon from selling its infringing product and forcing it to hand over its source code to IBM; this led to the cessation of operations at Neon.
In December 2013, Winsopia and LzLabs entered into a consultancy services agreement, under which Winsopia agreed to perform discovery, quality assurance, and software development work for LzLabs. The court identified that Winsopia's use of IBM's licensed software was "
for the sole purpose of assisting LzLabs in its software development.
" The defendants explained that they had established clean room procedures to ensure compliance with the terms of the ICA during development of what became the central issue of the dispute, the software defined mainframe ("SDM"). Those included: (i) codes of conduct between Winsopia and LzLabs; and (ii) systems to record intercompany requests made concerning the mainframe software.
In 2016, LzLabs launched its SDM, which competes with IBM's mainframe software, offering a smaller, external, non-mainframe computer capable of executing batch processing tasks typically performed by a mainframe system. IBM became suspicious about the methods involved in SDM's development and in 2020 notified Winsopia that it intended to audit Winsopia's compliance with the terms of the ICA. When Winsopia declined the audit request, IBM commenced proceedings seeking a declaration that Winsopia's license had been lawfully terminated and an injunction preventing Winsopia from making any further use of IBM's licensed software.
The Court's Decision
There were several issues for the court's determination, which were delivered over a
253-page decision
(see paragraph 138). These issues included assessing the proper construction of the ICA, the alleged breaches (and procurement of such breaches), and whether the acts alleged to be in breach of the ICA fell within the rights conferred by the Software Directive, as implemented by the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988 ("CDPA"), and whether these acts could be restricted or prohibited by contract.
This case summary focuses on the above-mentioned issues. However, further issues which were determined included assessing liability for the tort of unlawful means conspiracy, evaluating the validity of IBM's termination of the ICA and the determination of limitation periods in relation to IBM's claims. IBM was victorious in most issues.
At the consequentials hearing, the High Court ordered injunctive relief against the first, second, and sixth defendants, including prohibitions on the marketing, sale, and dissemination of the SDM software, and required delivery up or destruction of IBM’s ICA Programs, with compliance to be supervised by an independent forensic IT firm. The court awarded IBM its costs of the liability proceedings jointly against the first, second, and sixth defendants, with a payment on account of £20 million due by October

data.title: Tesla seeks to guard crash data from public disclosure
data.author: kklisura
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特斯拉的自动驾驶系统（FSD）、数据披露、安全问题以及竞争利益之间的冲突

不同观点：
• **数据披露与竞争利益的冲突**：[qwertox] 提到马斯克曾公开表示愿意开放专利以推动电动车技术，但现在特斯拉却以可能造成竞争损害为由，不愿公开可能拯救生命的数据。这引发了对特斯拉是否真正为技术进步着想的质疑。
• **车辆安全性与监管不足**：[isodev] 对特斯拉在碰撞检测方面的表现表示担忧，特别是当涉及安全气囊部署和事故认定时，认为监管不足。
• **自动驾驶系统的实际效果**：[Fischgericht] 分享了个人经历，指出特斯拉的自动驾驶系统在识别行人和物体方面的不足，认为隐藏 crash 数据是不明智的。
• **数据公开的公众权利**：[duxup] 认为，如果国家公路交通安全管理局（NHTSA）拥有数据，那么纳税人也应该有权访问这些数据。
• **事故责任与自动驾驶**：[mosdl] 提到一个涉及特斯拉自动驾驶功能的事故，指出事故责任尚未明确，但初步报告对特斯拉不利。

补充讨论：
• **自动驾驶技术的进步与体验**：[cowlby] 分享了使用特斯拉 FSD 功能的积极体验，特别是硬件和软件升级后的显著改善，认为这是值得每月支付99美元的安全功能。
• **EDR 数据与 ADS/ADAS 的区别**：[dhx] 解释了联合国和美国对车辆事件数据记录（EDR）的法规差异，指出这些数据主要记录车辆的物理行为，而非自动驾驶系统（ADS/ADAS）的操作细节。
• **媒体报道与利益冲突**：[jfoster] 提到《华盛顿邮报》对特斯拉的报道，指出该报的拥有者也拥有自动驾驶公司 Zoox，可能存在利益冲突。
• **对特斯拉自动驾驶的怀疑与支持**：[1vuio0pswjnm7] 提供了多个 NTSB 事故调查链接，质疑特斯拉的安全性。[nemothekid] 则认为很多事故是由于用户鲁莽驾驶，而非 FSD 系统本身的缺陷。[redm] 则强烈支持 FSD 技术，认为其技术进步令人惊叹。
• **公众数据与公共安全**：[7e] 主张公共道路上的数据应为公共数据，认为应该知道周围特斯拉车辆带来的风险。

争议焦点：特斯拉是否应公开涉及自动驾驶系统的 crash 数据，以保障公众安全，还是以保护商业利益为由拒绝披露。各方对特斯拉自动驾驶技术的安全性和可靠性存在明显分歧。
